body.text: Mahāpratisarā vidyārājñī
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>, the Queen of <s>Vidyās</s> (Spells)

body.text: namo bhagavatyai āryamahāpratisarāyai / namaḥ samyaksaṃbudhebhyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Homage to the blessed noble <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>. Homage to the perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s>.

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye bhagavān vajrameruśikharakuṭāgāre viharati sma / mahāvajrasamādhibhūmipratisthāne mahāvajrakalpavṛkṣasamalaṃkṛte / mahāvajrapuṣkiriṇīratnapadmaprabhodbhāsite / mahāvajravālikāsaṃskṛtabhūmibhāge / mahāvajrādhiṣṭhāne / mahāvajramaṇḍalamāḍe / śakrasya devānām indrasya bhavane / mahāvajrasiṃhāsanakoṭīniyutaśatasahasravirājite / dharmadeśanāpratibhānaprātihāryasamanvāgate / sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhite sarvadharmasamatāpraveśe sarvajñatāniryāte / caturaśītibhir bodhisatvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraiḥ sārdham / sarvair ekajātibhir avaivartikair anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau mahāsthāmaprāptair mahāvajravimokṣasamādhibuddhakṣetravikurvaṇamahāprātihāryasaṃdarśakaiḥ / ekacitrakṣaṇabhavamuhūrtasarvasatvacittacaritānupraveśavicitramadhurodāragambhīradharmadeśanāpratibhānaprātihāryasaṃdarśakair anekabuddhakṣetratathāgatamahāpūjameghārcanāvimokṣamukhadhāraṇīsamādhivaśitābhijñāvaeṇikabodhyaṅgamārgabhūmipāramitopāyakauśalyasaṃgrahavastramahāmaitrīkaruṇāmuditopekṣāmaitrībalaviviktaparyavadātacittasaṃtānaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in the pinnacle-hall on the summit of <s>Vajrameru</s>, at the great site established upon the ground of <s>vajra-samādhi</s>, adorned with great <s>vajra</s> wish-fulfilling trees, illuminated by the radiance of jewel-lotuses in the great <s>vajra</s> lotus-pond, on a ground-surface paved with great <s>vajra</s> sand, at the great <s>vajra</s> seat of authority, within the great <s>vajra</s> <s>maṇḍala</s> pavilion, in the palace of <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, resplendent with hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of great <s>vajra</s> lion-thrones, endowed with the miraculous display of eloquence in teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, blessed by the empowerment of all <s>Buddhas</s>, entered into the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>, proceeding from omniscience—together with eighty-four hundred thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, all in their last birth, irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), having attained great power, displaying the great miraculous feat of the <s>vajra</s> liberation <s>samādhi</s> and the transformation of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, displaying in a single moment of mind the miraculous feat of penetrating the varied conduct and thoughts of all beings and teaching the <s>Dharma</s> in a wondrous, sweet, noble, and profound manner, [endowed with] the approaches to the liberation of making great offering-clouds to <s>Tathāgatas</s> across innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields, <s>dhāraṇī</s>, <s>samādhi</s>, mastery, superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), unique qualities, factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅgas</s>), paths, stages (<s>bhūmis</s>), perfections (<s>pāramitās</s>), skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), means of gathering [disciples], great lovingkindness (<s>maitrī</s>), compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), the power of lovingkindness, and with mental continuums that are secluded, purified, and radiant.

body.text: tadyathā / vajragarbheṇa ca bodhisatvena mahāsatvena / vajranetreṇa ca / vajragātreṇa ca / vajramatinā ca / vajrahastena ca / vajrasaṃhatena ca / vajranārāyaṇena ca / vajravikurvitena ca / vajrakūtena ca / vajrarāśinā ca / vajrāṅkuśena ca / suvajreṇa ca / vajrasenena ca / vajraketunā ca bodhisatvena mahāsatvena //
body.translated_text: Namely, with the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s>, <s>Vajranetra</s>, <s>Vajragātra</s>, <s>Vajramati</s>, <s>Vajrahasta</s>, <s>Vajrasaṃhata</s>, <s>Vajranārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Vajravikurvita</s>, <s>Vajrakūṭa</s>, <s>Vajrarāśi</s>, <s>Vajrāṅkuśa</s>, <s>Suvajra</s>, <s>Vajrasena</s>, and the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Vajraketu</s>.

body.text: evaṃ pramukhair bodhisatvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃbahulaiś ca mahāśrāvakaiḥ sarvair arhadbhir kṣīṇāsravair ucchinnabhavasaṃyojanaiḥ
body.translated_text: Together with such leading hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and with many great <s>Śrāvakas</s>, all of whom were <s>Arhats</s>, with outflows destroyed, with the fetters of existence cut off,

body.text: samyagājñāsuvimuktacittaiḥ suvimuktaprajñair acintyasamādhibalaprātihāryavikurvaṇamahāsthāmaprāptair asaṅgajñānadarśibhiḥ / sarvair vigatamalair nidagdhasaṃkleśavāsanābījaiḥ //
body.translated_text: with minds well-liberated through perfect knowledge, with wisdom well-liberated, having attained great power through the miraculous displays of inconceivable <s>samādhi</s> power and transformation, possessing unobstructed knowledge and vision—all with defilements gone, with the seeds of the imprints of contamination burned away.

body.text: yadutāyuṣmatā ca śāradvatīputreṇa / āyuṣmatā ca pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputreṇa / āyuṣmatā ca kaphinena / āyuṣmatā ca subhūtinā / āyuṣmatā ca revatena / āyuṣmatā ca mahāmaudgalyāyanena / āyuṣmatā ca cundena / āyuṣmatā ca nandena / āyuṣmatā ca sunandena / āyuṣmatā ca kāśyapena / āyuṣmatā ca mahākāśyapena / āyuṣmatā ca nandīkāśyapena / āyuṣmatā coruvilvākāśyapena / āyuṣmatā ca gayākāśyapena //
body.translated_text: Namely, with the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s>, the venerable <s>Kaphina</s>, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the venerable <s>Revata</s>, the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, the venerable <s>Cunda</s>, the venerable <s>Nanda</s>, the venerable <s>Sunanda</s>, the venerable <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Nandīkāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Uruvilvākāśyapa</s>, and the venerable <s>Gayākāśyapa</s>.

body.text: evaṃ pramukhaiḥ saṃbahulair mahāśrāvakaiḥ sārdhaṃ maheśvaradevaputrapramukhaiś cāsaṃkhyeyair aparimāṇair anabhilāṣyānabhilāṣyaiḥ śuddhāvāsakayikair devaputraiḥ //
body.translated_text: Together with such leading great <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and with innumerable, immeasurable, indescribably indescribable divine sons of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abodes), headed by the divine son <s>Maheśvara</s>.

body.text: brahmaṇā ca sahāpatinā / brahmakāyikadevaputrapramukhair devaputraiḥ / suyāmena ca devaputreṇa / suyāmakāyikadevaputraparivāreṇa / saṃtuṣitena ca devaputraparivāreṇa / nirmāṇaratinā ca / paranirmitavaśavartinā ca / śakreṇa ca devānām indreṇa / sarvadevaputraparivāreṇa //
body.translated_text: And with <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>, with divine sons headed by the divine sons of <s>Brahmā's</s> retinue, with the divine son <s>Suyāma</s> and the retinue of the <s>Suyāma</s> divine sons, with the retinue of the <s>Saṃtuṣita</s> divine son, with the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> [gods], with the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> [gods], with <s>Śakra</s> lord of the gods, and with the retinue of all divine sons.

body.text: vemacitriṇā cāsurendreṇa / balinā ca / prahlādena ca / rāhunā ca / vairocanena ca / subāhunā ca / evaṃ pramukhair aparimitāprameyāsaṃkhyeyair asurendraiḥ //
body.translated_text: With the <s>Asura</s> lord <s>Vemacitrin</s>, <s>Bali</s>, <s>Prahlāda</s>, <s>Rāhu</s>, <s>Vairocana</s>, and <s>Subāhu</s>—with such leading limitless, immeasurable, innumerable <s>Asura</s> lords.

body.text: sāgareṇa ca nāgarājena / takṣakena ca / vāsukinā cā / śaṅkhapālena ca / karkoṭakena ca / padmena ca / mahāpadmena ca / evaṃ pramukhair aparimitāprameyāsaṃkhyeyair nāgarājaiḥ //
body.translated_text: With the <s>Nāga</s> king <s>Sāgara</s>, <s>Takṣaka</s>, <s>Vāsuki</s>, <s>Śaṅkhapāla</s>, <s>Karkoṭaka</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s>—with such leading limitless, immeasurable, innumerable <s>Nāga</s> kings.

body.text: drumeṇa ca kinnararājena / anekakinnaraparivāreṇa //
body.translated_text: With the <s>Kinnara</s> king <s>Druma</s> and the retinue of many <s>Kinnaras</s>.

body.text: pañcaśikhena ca gandharvarājena / anekagandharvarājaparivāreṇa ca //
body.translated_text: With the <s>Gandharva</s> king <s>Pañcaśikha</s> and the retinue of many <s>Gandharva</s> kings.

body.text: sarvārthasiddhena ca vidyādhararājena / anekavidyādhararājaparivāreṇa //
body.translated_text: With the <s>Vidyādhara</s> king <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> and the retinue of many <s>Vidyādhara</s> kings.

body.text: suparṇākṣeṇa ca garuḍarājena / anekagaruḍarājaparivāreṇa //
body.translated_text: With the <s>Garuḍa</s> king <s>Suparṇākṣa</s> and the retinue of many <s>Garuḍa</s> kings.

body.text: vaiśramaṇena ca / māṇibhadreṇa ca / pūrṇabhadreṇa ca / pāñcikena ca yakṣarājena / anekayakṣarājaparivāreṇa //
body.translated_text: With <s>Vaiśramaṇa</s>, <s>Māṇibhadra</s>, <s>Pūrṇabhadra</s>, and the <s>Yakṣa</s> king <s>Pāñcika</s>, together with the retinue of many <s>Yakṣa</s> kings.

body.text: hārītyā ca pañcaputraśataparivārayā / saptabhiś ca lokamātṛbhiḥ / saptabhiś ca mahārākṣasībhiḥ saptabhiś ca maharṣivaraiḥ / antarīkṣacaraiś ca sarvanakṣatragrahadevataiḥ / digbhiś ca vidigbhiś ca / pṛthivyā ca sarasvatyā ca / bhūtaiś ca vighnaiś ca vināyakaiś ca pretabhūtamaharddhikaiḥ / sarvaiś ca parvatarājaiḥ / varuṇena ca lokapālena / sarvasamudradevatāparivāreṇa / virūḍhakena ca virūpākṣeṇa ca daṇḍapāṇinā ca / naigutena ca / jātavedasā ca / saptabhiś ca mahāvāyubhiḥ / īśānena ca sapatnikena / anekagaṇakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparivāreṇa //
body.translated_text: With <s>Hārītī</s> accompanied by her five hundred sons, with the seven world-mothers, with seven great <s>Rākṣasīs</s>, with seven supreme great sages (<s>Maharṣis</s>), with all the deities of the <s>nakṣatras</s> (constellations) and planets moving through the sky, with the cardinal and intermediate directions, with <s>Pṛthivī</s> (Earth) and <s>Sarasvatī</s>, with <s>Bhūtas</s>, obstacles (<s>Vighnas</s>), and <s>Vināyakas</s>, with <s>Pretas</s> and <s>Bhūtas</s> of great supernatural power, with all the mountain kings, with <s>Varuṇa</s> the world-guardian and the retinue of all ocean deities, with <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s>, <s>Naiguta</s>, and <s>Jātavedas</s>, with the seven great winds, and with <s>Īśāna</s> together with his consort and the retinue of many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of hosts.

body.text: nārāyaṇena ca saparivāreṇa / dantakena ca dāmakena ca lohakena ca mohakena ca / mahāgaṇapatinā ca / megholkena ca / vināyakendreṇa ca / anekavighnavināyakaparivāreṇa //
body.translated_text: With <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and his retinue, with <s>Dantaka</s>, <s>Dāmaka</s>, <s>Lohaka</s>, and <s>Mohaka</s>, with the great <s>Gaṇapati</s>, <s>Megholka</s>, and the lord of <s>Vināyakas</s>, together with the retinue of many obstacle-<s>Vināyakas</s>.

body.text: ṣaṣṭyā ca koṭagiryā ca catasṛbhiś ca bhaginībhiḥ sabhrātṛkābhiḥ //
body.translated_text: With the sixty [goddesses], with <s>Koṭagirī</s>, and with the four sisters along with their brothers.

body.text: vajrāṅkuśyā ca / vajraśaṅkarayā ca / catuḥṣaṣṭibhiś ca vajrahūtībhiḥ / vajrasenena ca subāhunā ca / mūrdhaṭakena ca / anekavajrakulaparivāreṇa //
body.translated_text: With <s>Vajrāṅkuśī</s>, <s>Vajraśaṅkarā</s>, and the sixty-four <s>Vajrahūtīs</s>, with <s>Vajrasena</s>, <s>Subāhu</s>, and <s>Mūrdhaṭaka</s>, together with the retinue of many of the <s>Vajra</s> family.

body.text: tad anyaiś ca buddhadharmasaṃghābhiprasannaiḥ / aparimitāprameyāsaṃkhyeyair devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragabhūtapretapiśāconmārdāpasmārasādhyasāhillakoṣṭarakaiḥ //
body.translated_text: And with others devoted to the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>—limitless, immeasurable, innumerable <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, <s>Bhūtas</s>, <s>Pretas</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, <s>Unmādas</s>, <s>Apasmāras</s>, <s>Sādhyas</s>, <s>Sāhillas</s>, and <s>Koṣṭarakas</s>.

body.text: sūryeṇa ca devaputreṇa / candreṇa ca devaputreṇa / sucandreṇa ca devaputreṇa / sandhyayā ca devatayā / uṣasā ca devatayā / sarvaiś ca gantubhiḥ / rodasinyā ca devatayā / prajāpatyā ca devatayā sārdham //
body.translated_text: With the divine son <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun), the divine son <s>Candra</s> (Moon), the divine son <s>Sucandra</s>, the deity <s>Sandhyā</s> (Twilight), the deity <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn), all the celestial beings, the deity <s>Rodasinī</s>, and together with the deity <s>Prajāpatī</s>.

body.text: ity api ca bhagavān supravartitadharmacakraḥ supariniṣṭhitabuddhakāryaḥ suparipūrṇapuṇyajñānasaṃbhāraḥ suparigṛhītasarvajñatāmahābodhipāramitābhūmilābhojjvalitadvātriṃśatmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇālaṃkṛtaśarīraś
body.translated_text: Moreover, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who had well set in motion the wheel of the <s>Dharma</s>, who had well completed the task of a <s>Buddha</s>, who had well fulfilled the accumulations of merit and knowledge, who had fully embraced omniscience, whose body was blazing with the attainment of the stages of the great perfection of <s>Bodhi</s> and adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being (<s>mahāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇas</s>),

body.text: caturaśītyanuvyañjanavirājitaḥ sarvāṅgāvayavaśobhaḥ sarvasatvānavalokitamūrdhānirjitaḥ sarvamārakarmakovidaḥ sarvasatvajñānapañcavidhacakṣuḥ sarvākāravaropetaḥ sarvajñajñānasamanvāgataḥ sarvabuddhadharmasamanvāgataḥ / sarvamāraparapramādikugaṇigaṇapramathana udgatakīrtiśabdaśloka ārṣabhasiṃhanādaṃnadī samucchinnāvidyāndhakāro 'saṃkhyeyāparimāṇakoṭīniyutaśatasahasradānaśīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñopāyabalapraṇidhānapāramitāduṣkaracaryāvinivartitadvātriṃśatmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇacaturaśītyanuvyañjanagātraśobhaḥ / mahāvajraratnapadmagarbhasiṃhāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ / anekavajraratnavedikāsaṃskṛtapādapīṭhasupratiṣṭhite / anekavajraratnamakaramukhodgīrṇalohitamuktāvalīnibaddhagandhāyake / anekavajraratnamuktakiṅkiṇījālakalukalonnādite / anekavajraratnakarṇikāvilagnakarketanamahākarketanendranīlapuṣparāgaraśmijālāvabhāsitasamantaprasādike / anekavajraratnaśalākāvibhūṣitoddaṇḍātapatrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrakṛtacchāyāparikare / anekakalpavṛṣadrumopaśobhitavistāre sumerumātre vajraratnapadmāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ / kāñcanaparvatarāja iva śriyā jvalanasūryasahasrābhir ekaprabhāmaṇḍalavirājita bhūmibhāgaḥ / suparipūrṇacandramaṇḍala iva sarvalokapriyadarśano mahākalpavṛkṣa iva buddhadharmaiḥ saṃkusumito dharmaṃ deśayati sma //
body.translated_text: resplendent with eighty-four secondary marks (<s>anuvyañjanas</s>), beautiful in all limbs and members, unconquered with a head unseen by all beings, skilled in [overcoming] all works of <s>Māra</s>, possessing the five types of eyes (<s>cakṣus</s>) of the knowledge of all beings, endowed with all the finest qualities, possessing omniscient knowledge, endowed with all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, crushing the hosts of all <s>Māras</s>, adversaries, and negligent evil groups, with risen fame, renown, and glory, roaring the lion's roar of a supreme being (<s>ṛṣabha</s>), having severed the darkness of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), with bodily splendor of the thirty-two marks of a great being and eighty-four secondary marks produced through innumerable, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of difficult practices of the perfections of generosity (<s>dāna</s>), morality (<s>śīla</s>), patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), skillful means (<s>upāya</s>), power (<s>bala</s>), and aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>)—seated upon a great <s>vajra</s> jewel-lotus-womb lion-throne, well established upon a footstool adorned with many <s>vajra</s>-jewel balustrades, fragrant with garlands of red pearls streaming from the mouths of many <s>vajra</s>-jewel <s>makaras</s>, resounding with the tinkling of nets of many <s>vajra</s>-jewel pearl bells, illuminating all around with radiant nets of rays from sapphires and rubies adorning the great <s>karketana</s> [gems] affixed to many <s>vajra</s>-jewel bases, surrounded by the shade of hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of raised parasols decorated with many <s>vajra</s>-jewel rods, in a vast [setting] adorned with many wish-fulfilling trees—seated upon a <s>vajra</s>-jewel-lotus throne the size of <s>Sumeru</s>, like a golden mountain king blazing with glory, with its ground-area resplendent with the radiance of a single halo equal to a thousand suns, beautiful to behold for all the world like a fully round moon-disc, blossoming with <s>Buddha</s>-qualities like a great wish-fulfilling tree—he was teaching the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇaṃ paryavasāne kalyāṇaṃ svarthaṃ suvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ saṃprakāśayati sma //
body.translated_text: good in the beginning, good in the middle, good at the end, with good meaning, with good phrasing, complete, perfect, pure, and stainless — he illuminated the holy life.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān mūrdhna ūrṇakeśāt sarvabuddhasaṃdarśanaṃ nāma raśmijālaṃ pramuñcati sma / tena ca raśmijvālenāyaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātur avabhāsitaḥ / sphuṭīkṛto 'bhūt / yāvanti ca gaṅgānadīvālukopamāni buddhakṣetrāṇi tāni ca sarvāṇi tenāvabhāsena sphuṭīkṛtāny avabhāsitāny abhūvan / ye ca teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu buddhā bhagavanto 'nekasiṃhāsanakoṭīniyutaśatasahasravyūhakūṭāgāravimāneṣu dharmaṃ darśayati sma / sārdhaṃ
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One released from the <s>ūrṇā</s>-hair on the crown of his head a net of light rays called 'Vision of All Buddhas.' By that blaze of light, this great trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu</s>) was illuminated and made radiant. And as many Buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> — all of those were likewise illuminated and made radiant by that light. And the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> in those Buddha-fields were teaching the <s>Dharma</s> in palace mansions adorned with many millions of billions of hundreds of thousands of lion-thrones, together with

body.text: mahāśrāvakair bodhisatvair bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikābhir devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaiḥ sārdham //
body.translated_text: great disciples (<s>mahāśrāvaka</s>), <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃs tāṃ vistīrṇāṃ pariṣadām āmantrayate sma //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed that vast assembly:

body.text: athāto mahāpratisarāṃ mahāvidyāṃ pravakṣāmi sarvasatvānukampayā /
body.translated_text: "Now I shall proclaim the great <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>, the great <s>vidyā</s>, out of compassion for all beings.

children.translated_text: This <s>dhāraṇī</s> crushes all evils and destroys all malevolent [forces].
By merely hearing it, sins are utterly destroyed.
She bestows happiness upon all beings and liberates from all diseases.
Out of compassion for all beings, she was spoken by the Protector of the World.
For the protection of all embodied beings who have committed evil deeds —
one who is protected by her may even enter the abode of the <s>asuras</s>.

children.text: aḍakavatīṃ tathā gacched yakṣāṇām ālayaṃ bhuvi /
children.translated_text: One may likewise go to <s>Aḍakavatī</s>, the abode of the <s>yakṣas</s> on earth,
into the terrible and fierce battle of <s>bhūtas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, and <s>piśācas</s>.
One becomes invincible to all enemies and all hosts of <s>bhūtas</s>.
All planetary influences (<s>graha</s>) are destroyed by the recitation and proclamation of [her] name.
<s>Skandha</s>-spirits, madness-spirits, epilepsy-demons, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>ḍākinī</s>-spirits,
vitality-devourers of great power — they harm the human race.

children.text: te sarve stambhitā bhonti pratisarāyās tu tejasā /
children.translated_text: All of them become paralyzed by the power of <s>Pratisarā</s>,

children.text: paracakrā vinaśyanti kākhordā ye ca dāruṇāḥ //
children.translated_text: and hostile armies are destroyed, as well as the terrible sorcerers (<s>kākhorda</s>).

children.text: mantrakarmā na bādhante mūlakarmāc ca mucyate /
children.translated_text: Mantra-rituals cannot harm [the bearer], and one is freed from root-sorcery (<s>mūlakarma</s>).

children.text: na viṣaṃ na garaṃ nāgnir na śastraṃ naiva codakam //
children.translated_text: Neither poison, nor venom, nor fire, nor weapons, nor even water,

children.text: aśanir vidyutaś caiva kālavāyur na bādhate /
children.translated_text: neither thunderbolt nor lightning, nor the wind of death can harm [the bearer].
One crushes all enemies by the power of this queen of <s>vidyās</s>.

children.text: upasargā vinaśyanti vyādhayo na bhavanty api /
children.translated_text: Calamities are destroyed and diseases do not arise.

children.text: sarve 'rthās tasya sidhyanti jayaṃ prāpnoti nityaśaḥ //
children.translated_text: All one's purposes are accomplished, and one always attains victory.

children.text: yaḥ kaścid dhārayed vidyāṃ kaṇṭhe bāhau ca nityaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whoever constantly wears this <s>vidyā</s> on the neck or on the arm —

children.text: tasya sarvāṇi kāryāṇi sidhyante nātra saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: all that person's endeavors succeed; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: nityaṃ rakṣanti devendrā nāgarājās tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods, constantly protects [such a person], and likewise the <s>Nāga</s> kings,
the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of great vigor, the <s>Buddhas</s>, and the solitary leaders (<s>pratyekanāyaka</s>),
the disciples of all the <s>Buddhas</s>, and the <s>vidyā</s>-goddesses of great power —
they constantly perform protection for the bearer of <s>Pratisarā</s>.

children.text: vajrapāṇiś ca yakṣendro rājānaś caturas tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, lord of the <s>yakṣas</s>, and the four kings likewise —

children.text: tasya rakṣāṃ kariṣyanti divā rātrau na saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: they will protect that person day and night; there is no doubt.

children.text: śakraś ca trideśaiḥ sārdhaṃ brahmā viṣṇur maheśvarāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> together with the thirty-three [gods], <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>,
<s>Nandikeśa</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Kārtikeya</s>, <s>Gaṇeśvara</s>,
all the hosts of divine mothers, and other beings of <s>Māra</s>'s retinue,

children.text: ṛṣayaś ca mahātejā devāś caiva maharddhikāḥ //
children.translated_text: and the great sages (<s>ṛṣi</s>) of great power, and the gods of great supernatural ability —
they will constantly protect the bearer of <s>Pratisarā</s>.
The great-souled <s>Buddhas</s> and the <s>vidyā</s>-goddesses of great power,
of great vigor, great brilliance, and great strength and valor —
<s>Māmakī</s> and <s>Bhṛkuṭī</s>, the goddess <s>Tārā</s>, and <s>Aṅkuśī</s>,
<s>Vajrasaṃkalā</s>, <s>Śvetā</s>, and <s>Mahāśvetā</s> likewise,

children.text: mahākālī ca dūtyaś ca vajradūtyas tathāparāḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Mahākālī</s>, and the female messengers, and the <s>Vajra</s>-messengers, and others besides,
<s>Supāśī</s>, <s>Vajrapāśī</s>, <s>Cakrapāṇi</s> of great strength,
<s>Vajramālā</s>, the great <s>vidyā</s>, and likewise <s>Amṛtakuṇḍalī</s>,
<s>Aparājitā</s>, the great goddess, <s>Kālakarṇī</s> of great power,

children.text: tathā dhanyā mahābhāgā padmakuṇḍalir eva ca //
children.translated_text: and the blessed <s>Dhanyā</s> of great fortune, and <s>Padmakuṇḍalī</s>,
<s>Puṣpadantī</s>, <s>Maṇicūḍā</s>, <s>Svarṇakeśī</s>, and <s>Piṅgalā</s>,
the great goddess of great brilliance, <s>Dhanyā</s>, and <s>Vidyunmālinī</s>,
the <s>rākṣasī</s> <s>Ekajaṭā</s> and <s>Buddhākṣitikanāyikā</s>,
the blessed <s>Kāpālinī</s> of great fortune, and <s>Dhanyā</s>, and <s>Laṅkeśvarī</s>,
and many other <s>vidyā</s>-[goddesses] who act for the benefit of beings —

children.text: tasya rakṣāṃ kariṣyanti yasya vidyā kare sthitā //
children.translated_text: they will protect the one in whose hand this <s>vidyā</s> abides.
<s>Hārītī</s> and <s>Pāñcika</s>, <s>Śaṅkhinī</s>, <s>Kūṭadantinī</s>,

children.text: śrīdevī sarasvatī caiva taṃ rakṣanti sadānugāḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīdevī</s> and <s>Sarasvatī</s> — they protect [the bearer] as constant companions.

children.text: mahāpratisarām etāṃ yā strī dhārayate sadā /
children.translated_text: Whatever woman constantly bears this <s>Mahāpratisarā</s> —
all accomplishments (<s>siddhi</s>) will be hers, and she will always be blessed with children in the womb.

children.text: sukhaṃ garbhāṇi vardhante sukhaṃ prasūyati gurviṇī /
children.translated_text: Pregnancies develop happily, and the expectant mother gives birth with ease.

children.text: vyādhayaś cāpi naśyanti sarvapāpā na saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Diseases are destroyed, as are all sins — there is no doubt.
One becomes meritorious and powerful; wealth and grain increase.
One's words become authoritative, and one will be worthy of veneration.

children.text: śucir dvārayate yas tu striyo vā puruṣo 'tha vā /
children.translated_text: Whoever wears it with purity — whether woman or man —
that person will become, from among all beings, [a companion] of the Lord of Liberation.

body.text: sukhitaś ca bhaven nityaṃ sarvavyādhivivarjitam //
body.translated_text: One will always be happy, free from all diseases.

body.text: rājāno vaśagās tasya sāntaḥpuramahājanāḥ //
body.translated_text: Kings become subject to that person, along with their inner court and great assemblies.

children.text: nityaṃ ca jvalate lakṣmyā puṇyarāśir vivardhate /
children.translated_text: One constantly blazes with prosperity (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), and the heap of merit increases.
All ritual purposes (<s>kalpa</s>) are accomplished for that person, who has entered every <s>maṇḍala</s>.
That person becomes a knower of all <s>samaya</s> vows, in accordance with the word of the <s>Jina</s>.
Bad dreams do not afflict [the bearer]; all sins are completely removed.

children.text: kilbiṣāś caiva naśyanti pratyamitrās tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Transgressions are destroyed, and likewise adversaries.
For the destruction of all planetary influences, it was spoken by the lords of wisdom.

children.text: sarvakāmaṃgamā hy eṣā bhāvayed yas tu nityaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: This [<s>vidyā</s>] fulfills all desires; whoever cultivates it constantly —

children.text: tad idānīṃ pravakṣāmi bhūtasaṃghā śṛṇontu me //
children.translated_text: I shall now proclaim it: let the hosts of <s>bhūtas</s> listen to me!

body.text: namo buddhāya / namo dharmāya / namo saṃghāya / namaḥ sarvatathāgatānāṃ namo namaḥ / namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisatvadharmasaṃghebhyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>! Homage to the <s>Dharma</s>! Homage to the <s>Saṃgha</s>! Homage, homage to all the <s>Tathāgatas</s>! Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃghas</s>!

body.translated_text: Protect me together with my retinue and all beings everywhere, O purifier of all evil! <s>huru huru muru muru</s>, protect, protect me and all helpless, unprotected, refugeless beings! Liberate them from all sufferings! O fierce one, fierce one, ferocious one, swift one, averter of all evil-doers! O victory-bearer! <s>huru huru muru muru curu curu turu turu</s>, O protector of life, crusher of the foremost gods! Worshipped by all hosts of gods! <s>cili cili dhili dhili</s>, O one who gazes in all directions! O radiant one, supremely radiant, purified in supreme radiance, purifier of all evil! <s>dhuru dhuru</s>, O bearer of the earth, hold, hold! <s>sumu sumu musu musu</s>, O shining one, shake all evil-doers! Fulfill for me, O purifier of all evil, my wish! O glorious bearer of wealth, victory-lotus! <s>kṣiṇi kṣiṇi</s>, O goad that grants boons! <s>oṃ</s>, O one purified by the lotus! Purify, purify, O pure one, pure one! Fill, fill! <s>bhiri bhiri bhuru bhuru</s>, O one purified in auspiciousness! O one with a sanctified face! O sword-bearer, sword-bearer! <s>khara khara</s>, O blazing-peaked one! O one whose radiance gazes in all directions! O one purified in supreme radiance! O one purified in the light shed in all directions! Blaze, blaze, O attractor of all gods! O one true to your vow! <s>oṃ hrītraṃ tara tara</s>, deliver, deliver me and all beings! O one beheld by the <s>Nāgas</s>! <s>lahu lahu hulu hulu hutu hutu turu turu kiṇi kiṇi kṣiṇi kṣiṇi huni huni</s>, O devourer of all seizers! O tawny one, tawny one! <s>muru muru mucu mucu musu musu musuri</s>, O delighted one! Cross, cross, O one beheld by the <s>Nāgas</s>! Deliver, O <s>Bhagavatī</s>, from these greatly terrifying fears! Everywhere, completely, with a <s>vajra</s> (diamond) wall and <s>vajra</s> noose binding, O one purified in <s>vajra</s> flame! <s>bhuri bhuri</s>, O <s>Bhagavatī</s>, purifier of the womb! O fulfiller of the belly! Blaze, blaze, shake, shake, O blazing one! May the gods rain down everywhere with divine waters! O showerer of the nectar of immortality, O one who causes the descent of deities! May they consecrate me with the nectar of the excellent words of the <s>Sugatas</s>, with their excellent bodies! Protect, protect me always and everywhere, from all fears, from all calamities, from all misfortunes, from all diseases, from all terrors of evil beings! O purifier of all quarrels, disputes, conflicts, contentions, bad dreams, ill omens, inauspiciousness, and evil! O destroyer of all <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and <s>nāgas</s>! Shake, shake, O powerful one! Conquer, conquer, be victorious, be victorious! May there be victory always and everywhere! May this <s>vidyā</s> (spell) succeed for me! Accomplish the <s>maṇḍala</s>! Strike down the obstacles! Conquer, conquer, succeed, succeed, be accomplished, be accomplished, be awakened, be awakened! Fulfill, fulfill, O fulfiller, fulfiller! Fulfill my wish, O one whose form arises from all <s>vidyās</s>! O supreme victorious one, O victory-maker, O victorious one! Abide, abide, O <s>Bhagavatī</s>! Guard the pledge! O one purified by the heart of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, look upon me together with my retinue and all beings,

body.text: cātha mahādāruṇabhayeṣu sarvāsāṃ paripūraya trāyasva mahābhayebhyaḥ / sara 2 prasara 2 sarvāvaraṇaviśodhani samantākāramaṇḍalaviśuddhe / vigate 2 vigatamale / sarvamalaviśodhani / sarvāmaṅgalaviśuddhe / sarvāmaṅgalaviśodhani / kṣiṇi 2 sarvapāpaviśuddhe / malavigate / jayavati tejovati vajravati trailokyādhiṣṭhite svāhā //
body.translated_text: and in these greatly terrifying dangers, fulfill all wishes! Save from the great fears! <s>sara sara prasara prasara</s>, O purifier of all obscurations, O one purified in the <s>maṇḍala</s> of complete form! O one free from impurity, free from impurity! O purifier of all impurity! O one purified of all inauspiciousness! O purifier of all inauspiciousness! <s>kṣiṇi kṣiṇi</s>, O one purified of all evil! O one free from stain! O victorious one, O radiant one, O <s>vajra</s>-bearing one, O one empowered over the three worlds, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: sarvatathāgatamūrdhābhiṣikte svāhā //
body.translated_text: To the one consecrated on the crown by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: sarvabuddhabodhisatvābhiṣikte svāhā //
body.translated_text: To the one consecrated by all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: sarvatathāgatahṛdayaviśuddhe svāhā //
body.translated_text: To the one purified by the heart of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: sarvatathāgatābhiṣikte svāhā //
body.translated_text: To the one consecrated by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: sarvatathāgatahṛdayādhiṣṭhitahṛdaye svāhā //
body.translated_text: To the one whose heart is empowered by the heart of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: sarvatathāgatahṛdayasiddhe svāhā //
body.translated_text: To the one accomplished through the heart of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: indre indravati indravyavalokite / brahme brahmādhyuṣite svāhā //
body.translated_text: To <s>Indra</s>, to <s>Indravatī</s>, to the one beheld by <s>Indra</s>! To <s>Brahmā</s>, to the one in whom <s>Brahmā</s> dwells, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: viṣṇunamaskṛte svāhā / maheśvaravanditapūjitāyai svāhā //
body.translated_text: To the one honored by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the one venerated and worshipped by <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: vajradhara vajrapāṇibalavīryādhiṣṭhite svāhā //
body.translated_text: To the one empowered by the strength and vigor of <s>Vajradhara</s> and <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: dhṛtarāṣṭrāye svāhā / virūḍhakāya svāhā / virūpākṣāya svāhā / vaiśramaṇāya svāhā / caturmahārājanamaskṛtāya svāhā //

body.text: nāgavilokitāya svāhā / devagaṇebhyaḥ svāhā / nāgagaṇebhyaḥ svāhā / yakṣagaṇebhyaḥ svāhā / rākṣasagaṇebhyaḥ svāhā / gandharvagaṇebhyaḥ svāhā / asuragaṇebhyaḥ svāhā / garuḍagaṇebhyaḥ svāhā / kinnaragaṇebhyaḥ svāhā / mahoragagaṇebhyaḥ svāhā / manuṣyagaṇebhyaḥ svāhā / amanuṣyagaṇebhyaḥ svāhā //

To the hosts of <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the hosts of <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the hosts of <s>mahoragas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the hosts of humans, <s>svāhā</s>! To the hosts of non-humans, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: śāntibhyaḥ svāhā / puṣṭibhyaḥ svāhā / svastyayanebhyaḥ svāhā //
body.translated_text: To the pacifications, <s>svāhā</s>! To the nourishments, <s>svāhā</s>! To the blessings of well-being, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: śivaṃkari svāhā / śaṃkari svāhā / śāntiṃkari svāhā / puṣṭiṃkari svāhā / balavardhani svāhā / balavardhanaṃkari svāhā / śrīkari svāhā / śrīvardhani svāhā / śrījvālini svāhā / muci svāhā / namuci svāhā / muruci svāhā / vegavati svāhā //

O one blazing with prosperity, <s>svāhā</s>! O liberator, <s>svāhā</s>! O <s>Namuci</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! O radiant one, <s>svāhā</s>! O swift one, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: oṃ muni 2 vimuni 2 dhari cari calane bhayavigate bhayahariṇi / bodhi 2 bodhaya 2 buddhili 2 sarvatathāgatahṛdayajuṣṭe svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>oṃ muni muni vimuni vimuni dhari cari calane</s>, O one free from fear, O remover of fear! Awaken, awaken, enlighten, enlighten, <s>buddhili buddhili</s>, O one sustained by the heart of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: oṃ muni 2 munivare abhisiñcantu māṃ sarvasatvāṃś ca sarvatathāgatāḥ sarvavidyābhiṣekair mahāvajrakavacamudrāmudritaiḥ sarvatathāgatahṛdayādhiṣṭhitavajre svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>oṃ muni muni</s>, O supreme sage! May all <s>Tathāgatas</s> consecrate me and all beings with the consecrations of all <s>vidyās</s>, sealed with the seal of the great <s>vajra</s> armor! O <s>vajra</s> empowered by the heart of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: samantajvālāmālāviśuddhisphūritacintāmaṇimahāmūdrāhṛdayāparājitā mahādhāraṇī tena khalu samayena tasyām eva pariṣadi mahābrāhmaṇaḥ saṃnipatito 'bhūt / saṃniṣaṇṇaś ca //
body.translated_text: [This is] the invincible great <s>dhāraṇī</s>, the heart of the great mudrā of the wish-fulfilling jewel, radiating the purification of the garland of universal flames (<s>Samantajvālāmālāviśuddhisphūritacintāmaṇimahāmudrāhṛdayāparājitā Mahādhāraṇī</s>). At that time, in that very assembly, a great <s>brāhmaṇa</s> had gathered and was seated.

body.text: tatra bhagavān mahābrāhmaṇam āmantrayate sma / asyā mahāpratisarāyā mahāvidyārājñaḥ sahasravarṇamātreṇa mahābrāhmaṇa tasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhitur vā sarvapāpavinirmuktir bhavati / yasya punar iyaṃ hṛdayagatā bhaviṣyati / sa mahābrāhmaṇa vajrakāya iti veditavyaḥ / nāgnis tasya kāye kramiṣyati / kim iti saṃjñitaṃ / yadā kapilavastumahānagaravare rāhulabhadraḥ kumāro mātuḥ kukṣigato 'bhūd yadā ṣaḍvarṣātikrānte sarvārthasiddhena kumāreṇa mama nābhiḥ pādaṃ suṣṭhena pṛṣṭho nirgatas tad ājānāmi / nānyat kiṃcid iti / parikīrṇāgninā viṣodakena taptakuṭhārikayāturayamānān atrāthāparājitā bhavāmi / tadā gopayā śākyakanyayā ātmānam agnikhadāyāṃ prakṣiptaḥ / tatra padminī prādurbhūtā / tadā rāhulabhadrakumāro mātuḥ kukṣigato eva imāṃ vidyāṃ manasy akarṣīt / asyā vidyāyā anusmaraṇamātreṇa
body.translated_text: Thereupon the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed <s>Mahābrāhmaṇa</s>: 'O <s>Mahābrāhmaṇa</s>, by the mere recitation of a thousand syllables of this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s>, that son or daughter of good family becomes completely freed from all sins. And whoever holds this [<s>vidyā</s>] in their heart — that person, O <s>Mahābrāhmaṇa</s>, should be known as having a vajra-body. Fire will not reach their body. How is this known? When in the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, the prince <s>Rāhulabhadra</s> was in his mother's womb — after six years had passed, prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> [the Buddha] departed, touching my navel with his foot and turning his back — I know this and nothing else. When I was being tormented by a surrounding fire, poisoned water, and heated axes, I was here invincible. At that time, <s>Gopā</s> the <s>Śākya</s> maiden threw herself into a fire pit, and there a lotus appeared. At that time, prince <s>Rāhulabhadra</s>, while still in his mother's womb, brought this <s>vidyā</s> to mind. By the mere recollection of this <s>vidyā</s>,

body.text: so 'pi tasmin kṣaṇe śītībhāvam udāgataḥ / tato gopāyāḥ śākyakanyāyāḥ śarīram agninā na spṛṣṭam / tat kasya hetor eṣā vidyā sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhitā / tena hetunāyaṃ mahābrāhmaṇo 'gnir na dahati / na ca viṣeṇa śakyaṃ taṃ jīvitād vyaparopayitum / tat katham iti //
body.translated_text: he too, in that instant, became cool. Therefore <s>Gopā</s> the <s>Śākya</s> maiden's body was not touched by fire. For what reason? This <s>vidyā</s> is empowered by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. For that reason, O <s>Mahābrāhmaṇa</s>, fire does not burn [one who holds it], nor can one be deprived of life by poison. How is that so?

body.text: yadā mahābrāhmaṇa śūrpārake mahānagaravare koṣavaṇikasya śreṣṭhinaḥ putro vidyāvādiko babhūva / tena tad vidyābalena takṣako nāgarājā ākarṣitaḥ / ākarṣayitvā ca pramāṇavaśād baddho nadānto yāvat tenāsau krodhād daṣṭaḥ / sa tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukāṃ vedanāṃ vedayati / yathā jānāmi ca me jīvitaṃ niruddham iti / tatra bahavo vādikā āhutāḥ / na ca kaścic chaknoti viṣaṃ cikitsitum / atha traiva śūrpārake mahānagaravare vimalaviśuddhir nāmopāsikā prativasati sma / mahākaruṇāsamanvāgatā tasya iyaṃ mahāvidyārājñī jihvāgre 'bhūt / sā tasyāntikam upasaṃkrāntā upasaṃkramyemāṃ mahāvidyāṃ pravartayāmāsa / sā tayaikavelāyām anusmṛtamātrayā nirviṣaṃ smṛtipratilabdhaṃ kṛtvā tato mahāvyasanāt parimocayitvā imām eva śuddhiputre mahāvidyāṃ hṛdayagatāṃ kārayati sma / yathā vidhivad anujñātam iti //
body.translated_text: O <s>Mahābrāhmaṇa</s>, in the great city of <s>Śūrpāraka</s>, there was a son of the merchant guild-master <s>Koṣavaṇika</s>, who was a practitioner of <s>vidyā</s>. By the power of that <s>vidyā</s>, he summoned the <s>Nāga</s> king <s>Takṣaka</s>. Having summoned him, he bound him by the force of his power, but [the <s>Nāga</s>], untamed, bit him out of anger. He experienced sharp, harsh, bitter pain, and thought: 'I know that my life is ending.' Many [<s>vidyā</s>] practitioners were called, but no one was able to cure the poison. Now, in that very great city of <s>Śūrpāraka</s> there lived a lay-woman named <s>Vimalaviśuddhi</s>, endowed with great compassion, who had this <s>Mahāvidyārājñī</s> on the tip of her tongue. She approached him, and having approached, she set forth this great <s>vidyā</s>. By her mere recollection of it at one time, she rendered the poison harmless, restored his awareness, and having freed him from that great calamity, she caused this same great <s>vidyā</s> to be established in the heart of her pure son, as it was properly authorized.

body.text: api ca mahābrāhmaṇa kiṃ parijñātam iti / bārāṇāsyāṃ mahānagaryām anupūrveṇānuvicaramāṇo rājā brahmadatta iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati / tasya prātisīmiko balacakrarājā caturaṅgabalakāyaṃ saṃnāhya bārāṇasīmahānagarīṃ parivārya vināśayitum ārabdhaḥ / tato rājñā brahmadattasyāmātyair niveditam / deva paracakreṇa nagaram apahṛtam / tataḥ kiṃ tu khalu vayam upāyaṃ kuryāmo yenaitat paracakraṃ vinaśyet / ājñāṃ prayaccha / rājā kathayati / alpotsukā bhavanto mā bhavata / asti mama mahāpratisarā nāma vidyārājñī / yenāham ihemaṃ caturaṅgabalakāyaṃ parājeṣyāmi / tathā kariṣyāmi / amātyāḥ śirasā praṇipatyocuḥ / kim idaṃ mahārāja nāsmābhiḥ kadācid api na śrutam iti / rājā prāha / aham idānīṃ pratyakṣaṃ darśanaṃ kariṣyāmi / atha sa rājā brahmadatto
body.translated_text: Moreover, O <s>Mahābrāhmaṇa</s>, what has been ascertained? In the great city of <s>Bārāṇasī</s>, wandering in due course, there was a king known as <s>Brahmadatta</s>. His neighboring king, a ruler of a mighty army, having marshaled a fourfold military force, surrounded the great city of <s>Bārāṇasī</s> and began to destroy it. Then King <s>Brahmadatta</s>'s ministers reported: 'Lord, the city has been seized by the enemy forces. What stratagem shall we employ so that this enemy force may be destroyed? Give the command.' The king said: 'Do not be anxious, gentlemen. I have a <s>vidyārājñī</s> called <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>, by which I shall defeat this fourfold army. I shall do so.' The ministers, bowing their heads, said: 'What is this, O great king? We have never heard of it.' The king said: 'I shall now demonstrate it before your very eyes.' Then King <s>Brahmadatta</s>,

body.text: nānāgandhodakena snātaḥ śirāḥ śucivastraṃ prāvṛtya imāṃ mahāpratisarāṃ mahāvidyārājñīṃ yathāvidhinābhilikhya śiraḥ keśe 'vasthāpya imām eva mahāvidyārājñīṃ kavacaṃ kṛtvā saṃgrāmamadhye 'vatīrya ekākinaiva sarvāsau caturaṅgabalakāyaḥ parājitaḥ / āmarditaś ca tāvad yāvac caraṇaṃ gataḥ / iti kṛtvāsau balacakrarājā mukta iti //
body.translated_text: having bathed in water scented with various fragrances, covered his head with clean cloth, wrote down this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s> according to the proper method, placed it in his hair on his head, made this very <s>Mahāvidyārājñī</s> into armor, descended alone into the midst of battle, and that entire fourfold army was defeated. They were crushed until they fled. Thus that king of the mighty army was released.

body.text: evaṃ hi mahābrāhmaṇa pratyakṣaṃ mahānubhāveyaṃ mahāvidyārājñī sarvatathāgatahṛdayamudrādhiṣṭhitā / pratyakṣam eveti dhārayitavyā / sarvatathāgatasamaiṣā draṣṭavyā / ye kecit paścime kāle paścime samaye alpāyuṣkānāṃ mandabhāgyānāṃ mandadhānyānaṃ parīttabhāgyānāṃ satvānām arthāya hitāya sukhāya draṣṭavyā / yaḥ kaścin mahābrāhmaṇa imāṃ mahāvidyārājñīṃ yathāvidhinā likhitvā bāhau kaṇṭhe dhārayiṣyati / sa sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhito veditavyaḥ / sarvatathāgatakāya iti veditavyaḥ / vajrakāya iti veditavyaḥ / sarvatathāgatadhātugarbha iti veditavyaḥ / sarvatathāgatanetra iti veditavyaḥ / jvālitārciśarīra iti veditavyaḥ / abhedyakavaca iti veditavyaḥ / sa sarvaśatrūṇāṃ pramathana iti veditavyaḥ / sarvapāpāvaraṇanirdahana iti veditavyaḥ / sarvanarakagativiśodhana iti veditavyaḥ / kim iti pūrvaṃ parijñātaṃ mahābrāhmaṇa anyatamasmiṃ pṛthivīpradeśe bhikṣuśrāddhas tathāgatakulaśikṣākhaṇḍako 'dattādāyī sukhādvārahārakaḥ saṃghikaṃ cāturdiśikaṃ staupikaṃ gaṇaprāptaṃ ca yad dravyaṃ tat paudgalikaṃ kṛtvā sarvam adhiṣṭhāya takṣayati / yāvad apareṇa samayena mahāvyādhinā pṛṣṭaḥ / sa mahatīṃ duḥkhāvedanām anubhavati / sa tapasvī atrāṇo 'parāyaṇo 'pratiśaraṇo mahāntasukrośaṇāśabdaṃ karoti / atha tasminn eva pṛthivīpradeśe upāsako brāhmaṇo prativasati / tena tac chabdaḥ śrutaḥ / śrutvā ca punar yena sa bhikṣus tenopasaṃkrānta upasaṃkramya tasya bhikṣor imāṃ mahāpratisarāṃ mahāvidyārājñīṃ likhitvā kaṇṭhe badhnāti sma / samanantarabaddhāyāṃ mahāpratisarāyāṃ mahāvidyārājñyāṃ tasya bhikṣoḥ sarvā vedanāḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Mahābrāhmaṇa</s>, this <s>Mahāvidyārājñī</s> is manifestly of great power, empowered by the heart-seal of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. She is to be upheld as directly manifest. She should be regarded as equal to all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. She should be regarded as being for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of beings of short lifespan, little fortune, scanty grain, and meager lot in the final age, in the final period. Whoever, O <s>Mahābrāhmaṇa</s>, having written this <s>Mahāvidyārājñī</s> according to proper method, will wear it on the arm or neck — that person should be known as empowered by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, should be known as the body of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, should be known as a vajra-body, should be known as the womb of the relics of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, should be known as the eye of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, should be known as one whose body blazes with radiance, should be known as having impenetrable armor, should be known as the crusher of all enemies, should be known as the burner of all sinful obscurations, should be known as the purifier of all paths to hell. How was this previously ascertained? O <s>Mahābrāhmaṇa</s>, in a certain region of the earth, a monk of faith, who had broken the training rules of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s lineage, a taker of what is not given, one who snatches through the door of pleasure, who took property belonging to the <s>Saṅgha</s>, to the community of the four directions, to <s>stūpas</s>, and to the congregation, making it personal, seized everything and wasted it. Then, after some time, he was afflicted by a great illness. He experienced great painful feelings. Helpless, without refuge, without recourse, without shelter, he uttered loud cries of distress. Now, in that very region of the earth, there lived a lay-follower, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. He heard that sound. Having heard it, he approached that monk, and having approached, he wrote this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s> and tied it around the monk's neck. Immediately upon the <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s> being tied, all that monk's painful feelings

body.text: praśāntāḥ sarvavyādhibhyaḥ parimuktaḥ svasthaḥ saṃvṛtta iti / tasyām eva rātryām atyayābhyupasthite smṛtipratilabdhaḥ kālagataḥ / tasminn eva kṣatravare utsṛṣṭo 'vīcau mahānarake upapannaḥ / tac ca tasya mṛtaśarīraṃ bhikṣubhiḥ kūṭe sthāpitam / sā ca tasya mahāpratisarā mahāvidyārājñī kaṇṭhe baddhaivāsthitā / samanantaropapannasya tasya bhikṣos tasminn avīcau mahānarake teṣāṃ nārakānāṃ satvānāṃ sarvaduḥkhavedanāḥ śāntāḥ / te ca nārakasatvāḥ sarvasukhasamarpitā abhūvan / ye ca te mahānta-āvicikā-agniskandhās te 'pi sarveṇa sarvam upaśāntā iti / atha te yamapuruṣā vismayam āpannā yamasya dharmarājasyemaṃ niścayaṃ vistareṇārocayati sma //
body.translated_text: were pacified, he was freed from all diseases, and became well. On that very night, having confessed his transgressions, having regained mindfulness, he died. Upon being released in that same realm, he was reborn in the great <s>Avīci</s> hell. His dead body was placed by monks on a funeral pyre. And that <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s> remained tied around his neck. Immediately upon that monk's rebirth in the great <s>Avīci</s> hell, all painful feelings of those hell-beings were pacified. Those hell-beings were endowed with all happiness. And those great fires of <s>Avīci</s> were completely and entirely extinguished. Then <s>Yama</s>'s attendants, struck with wonder, reported this matter in detail to <s>Yama</s> the King of <s>Dharma</s>:

children.translated_text: 'A wondrous thing, O Lord, is seen in the hell-confinement!

children.text: praśāntā dāruṇā duḥkhāḥ satvānāṃ karmajāś ca ye /
children.translated_text: The terrible sufferings of beings, born of their <s>karma</s>, are pacified!
Even those burning coals abiding in the bodies are pacified, as well as the torments of the embodied ones.

children.text: karapattrā na bādhante kṣuradhārā na sajjate /
children.translated_text: The saws do not torment, the razor-edges do not cut,
The iron <s>śālmalī</s> trees are broken, the iron cauldrons are pacified.

children.text: asipattrāvane pattrā na bādhante karmajā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the sword-leaf forest, the <s>karma</s>-born leaves no longer torment.

children.text: yamas tvaṃ dharmarājo 'si dharmeṇa śāsayase prajām //
children.translated_text: You, <s>Yama</s>, are the King of <s>Dharma</s>; by <s>Dharma</s> you govern the beings.

children.text: idaṃ tu kāraṇaṃ nālpam asmākaṃ vaktum arhasi /
children.translated_text: This cause is no small matter; you should tell us.'
Then that King of <s>Dharma</s>, righteous in soul, firm in <s>Dharma</s>,
Having heard these words from those whose compassionate nature was lost,

children.text: kim etat kathyatāṃ śīghraṃ kathaṃ tv iti vaco 'vadat //
children.translated_text: 'What is this? Speak quickly! How is this so?' — he spoke these words.
Then, of those wicked beings, <s>Yama</s>'s terribly cruel servants,
heard these words of <s>Yama</s>, the King of <s>Dharma</s>:
'O Lord, this great being has been born in the hell-confinement,

children.text: avīcir yasya nāmedaṃ tenāsau narakasaṃkaṭa ucyate //
children.translated_text: which is called <s>Avīci</s> — and by him this is called the hell-confinement.

children.text: karmāṇaṃ yasya vaicitryaṃ satvā ye hi sukhīkṛtam /
children.translated_text: Through the variety of his <s>karma</s>, those beings who were made happy —

children.text: sukhino hy eva sarvatra punar yānti surālayam //
children.translated_text: indeed being happy everywhere, they go again to the abode of the gods.'

children.text: yamo 'pi dharmarājā vai dṛṣṭvā vadati vismitaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s>, the King of <s>Dharma</s>, having seen this, spoke with wonder:

children.text: maharddhiko 'yaṃ mahac cāsya śarīraṃ pūrvo janmikam //
children.translated_text: 'This one is of great supernatural power, and great is his body from a former birth.'

children.text: yathā dhātuśatair vṛndaṃ stūpaṃ śobhati śāśvatam /
children.translated_text: Just as a <s>stūpa</s> adorned with hundreds of relics (<s>dhātu</s>) shines eternally,
so does the body of one who has the <s>Pratisarā</s> tied at the neck shine.

body.text: atha te narakapālā yakṣā yamasya dharmarājasya idaṃ vacanam abruvan / katham iyaṃ deva pratisarety ucyate / dharmarāja uvāca / pratipat smārayed yas tu sa na gacchati durgatiṃ sugatiṃ gacchate cāsau pratisarābhāvabhāvitaḥ / yūyaṃ narakapālā vai gacchatha puṣkarāvatīṃ / tad rakṣatha mahākūṭaṃ devataiḥ parivāritam / taṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvasarvasakheṣu maitracittā bhaviṣyatha / atha te yakṣā yamapuruṣā tasyām eva rātryāṃ puṣkarāvatīṃ gatāḥ /
body.translated_text: Then those hell-wardens, the <s>yakṣas</s> of <s>Yama</s> the Dharma-King, spoke these words: 'How, O Lord, is this called <s>Pratisarā</s>?' The Dharma-King (<s>Dharmarāja</s>) said: 'One who recalls the practice does not go to an evil destiny but goes to a happy destiny, being imbued with the nature of the <s>Pratisarā</s>. You hell-wardens, go to <s>Puṣkarāvatī</s>! Guard the great mound (<s>kūṭa</s>) surrounded by deities! Having seen it, you shall become friendly-minded toward all beings everywhere.' Then those <s>yakṣas</s>, the servants of <s>Yama</s>, went to <s>Puṣkarāvatī</s> that very night.

children.translated_text: They then saw there, near the royal capital,
that mound (<s>kūṭa</s>), enclosed all around with a single gate.
They saw a dead body with the <s>Pratisarā</s> tied at its neck.
<s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and <s>Kinnaras</s>
surrounding it on all sides, performing unsurpassed worship.

children.text: yāvat tasya ca tair yakṣaiḥ pratisarākūṭeti nāma sthāpitam //
children.translated_text: Thereupon those <s>yakṣas</s> gave it the name '<s>Pratisarākūṭa</s>' (the Pratisarā Mound).

body.text: atha te yakṣā punar āgatya yamasya dharmarājasyemaṃ niścayaṃ vistareṇārocayati sma / evam etad deva tvayābhihitaṃ / samanantarodite tasmin vacanaparyavasāne mahāsatvas taṃ nārakaṃ śarīraṃ vijahya trāyastriṃśeṣu deveṣūpapannaḥ / tena hetunā pratisarāpūrvīdevaputra ity ucyate / tena hi mahābrāhmaṇa parijñātavatī pūrvatas tasmād eveyaṃ mahāpratisarā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā likhitavyā yathāvidhinā nityaṃ śarīragatāṃ kṛtvā dhārayitavyā / sa nityaṃ sarvavyasanaduḥkhebhyaḥ parimucyate / sarvadurgatibhayabhairavebhya uttarati / na vidyutā śakyaṃ pātayitum / kim iti vidyutā parijñātam //
body.translated_text: Then those <s>yakṣas</s>, having returned, reported in detail this conclusion to <s>Yama</s> the Dharma-King: 'It is so, O Lord, as you have stated.' Immediately upon the conclusion of those words, the great being, having left that infernal body, was reborn among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods. For that reason, he is called <s>Pratisarāpūrvī Devaputra</s> (the divine son formerly [saved by] Pratisarā). 'Therefore, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, it has been fully known from the beginning. For this very reason, this <s>Mahāpratisarā</s> should be held, recited, and written, and according to the proper ritual, it should always be kept on the body. One is perpetually freed from all calamities and sufferings. One is delivered from all fears and terrors of evil destinies. One cannot be struck down by lightning. How is this known regarding lightning?'

body.text: pūrvaṃ mahābrāhmaṇa hiṅgumardane mahānagare vimalaśaṅkho nāma śreṣṭhī mahādhanakanakasamṛddhaḥ paripūrṇakośakośāgārasaṃpanno babhūva / sa mahāsārthavāha iti khyātavān / atha sa mahāsārthavāho yānapātram āsādya mahāsamudram avatīrṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: Formerly, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, in the great city of <s>Hiṅgumardana</s>, there was a merchant (<s>śreṣṭhī</s>) named <s>Vimalaśaṅkha</s>, endowed with great wealth, gold, and prosperity, possessing full treasuries and storehouses. He was renowned as a great caravan leader (<s>mahāsārthavāha</s>). Then that great caravan leader, having obtained a ship, descended into the great ocean.

body.text: yāvat timiṅgilaiḥ so 'sya poto 'vastabdhaḥ vināśayitukāmā nāgāś ca saṃkṣubdhā mahāntagarjanā sphoṭaṃ kurvanti / vidyudulkām utsṛjanti vajrāśaniṃ pravarṣitum ārabdhāḥ / tatas te vaṇijo mahatā duḥkhenābhyāhatacittās taṃ mahāntaṃ nāgasaṃkṣobhaṃ vidyudulkāṃ vajrāśaniṃ cotsṛjanti taiś ca timiṅgilaiḥ potam avastabdhaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahāntaṃ utkrośanaṃ śabdaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ / te viśeṣair nāyācayanti / tatas te sārthavāhasyopagamya karuṇam idaṃ vacanam abruvan / paritrāyasva tvaṃ mahāsatva mocayāsmān mahābhayāt / atha khalu mahāsārthavāho dṛḍhacitto mahāmatiḥ vaṇijo viklavībhūtān idaṃ vacanam abruvat / mā bhair mā bhair vaṇijo bhavanto vīratāṃ vrajata / ahaṃ vo mocayiṣyāmy ato duḥkhamahārṇavāt / tata vīramānaso bhūtā vaṇija idaṃ vacanam abruvan / kim etat tena mahāsatva brūhi śīghram avighnataḥ / yāvad jīvitam asmākaṃ tvat prabhāvād mahāmate kathyatāṃ jñānamahātmyaṃ paścāt kiṃ kariṣyasi /
body.translated_text: Thereupon <s>timiṅgilas</s> (great sea monsters) seized his ship, intending to destroy it, and the <s>Nāgas</s>, stirred up, made great thunderous roars and explosions. They released lightning-bolts and began to rain down <s>vajra</s>-thunderbolts. Then those merchants, their minds stricken with great suffering, seeing the great disturbance of the <s>Nāgas</s>, the lightning-bolts and <s>vajra</s>-thunderbolts being released, and the ship seized by the <s>timiṅgilas</s>, began to make a great wailing cry. They prayed with special fervor. Then, approaching the caravan leader, they spoke these pitiful words: 'Save us, O great being! Free us from this great peril!' Then the great caravan leader, firm of mind and great of intellect, spoke these words to the terrified merchants: 'Fear not! Fear not, merchant friends! Be courageous! I shall free you from this ocean of great suffering.' Then the merchants, their spirits emboldened, spoke these words: 'What is it, O great being? Tell us quickly and without delay! As long as our lives endure, through your power, O great-minded one, declare the greatness of your knowledge — what will you do?'

children.text: tataḥ sārthapatis teṣām imāṃ vidyām udāharat /
children.translated_text: Then the caravan leader proclaimed to them this <s>vidyā</s>:

children.text: asti mama mahāvidyā pratisarā nāma viśrutā //
children.translated_text: 'I have a great <s>vidyā</s>, renowned by the name <s>Pratisarā</s>,
the crusher of all <s>Buddhas</s>, of great strength and valor.
With it I shall free [you] from this ocean of great suffering.'

body.text: tataḥ mahāsārthavāhas tasyāṃ velāyām imāṃ mahāpratisarāṃ mahāvidyārājñīṃ likhitvā dhvajāgrāvaropitāṃ karoti sma / samanantaraṃ dhvajāgrāvaropitāyām asyāṃ mahāpratisarāyāṃ mahāvidyārājñyāṃ sarva eva te timiṅgilās taṃ potam ekajvālībhūtaṃ paśyanti / tatas te nāgā maitramanasas teṣām antike 'vatīrya pūjāṃ kartum ārabdhāḥ / te ca timiṅgilā asyā mahāpratisarāyā mahāvidyārājñyā anubhāvena dahyamānāḥ / prapalāyitvā vilapaṃ gatāḥ / sārthikās tair mahānāgair mahati mahāratnadvīpe prāpitā iti //
body.translated_text: Then the great caravan leader, at that very moment, having written this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s> (Great Queen of Great Knowledge-Spells), raised it aloft on the top of a banner. Immediately upon this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s> being raised on the banner-top, all those <s>timiṅgilas</s> saw the ship as a single mass of flame. Then the <s>Nāgas</s>, becoming friendly-minded, descended near them and began to make offerings. Those <s>timiṅgilas</s>, burned by the power of this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s>, fled and went away lamenting. The merchants were brought by those great <s>Nāgas</s> to the great jewel island.

body.text: jñātavatīyaṃ mahāvidyā mahāpratisarā sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhitā tena hetunā mahābrāhmaṇa mahāvidyeti khyātā / tasmād avaśyam
body.translated_text: This great <s>vidyā</s> <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>, blessed by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, has been fully known. For that reason, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, it is renowned as <s>Mahāvidyā</s> (Great Knowledge-Spell). Therefore, it must certainly

body.text: eveyaṃ dhvajāgrāvaropitaṃ kṛtvā dhārayitavyā / sarvavātaśītākālameghavidyudaśanīṃ praśamayati / sarvadevamanuṣyāmanuṣyavigrahavivādeṣu parimocayati / sarvadaṃṣṭramaśakaśarabhakaprāṇakajātā vividharūpāḥ /sasyavināśakā na prabhavanti / praśamaṃ gacchanti / sarvaduṣṭacittā mṛgapakṣidaṃṣṭriṇo vinaśyanti / sarvāṇi ca puṣpaphalapattravanaspatyoṣadhisasyādīny abhivardhante / arasāni svādūni mṛdūni ca bhaviṣyanti / samyag eva paripācitāni bhaviṣyanti / ativṛṣṭyenāvṛṣṭidoṣāḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ na bhaviṣyanti / kālavṛṣṭir bhaviṣyanti nākālavṛṣṭiḥ / ye ca tasmin viṣaye mahānāgās te samyag eva kālena kālaṃ varṣadhārām utsṛjanti / yasmin viṣaye iyaṃ vidyārājñī mahāpratisarā nāma pracariṣyati / tatra taiḥ satvair jñātvā pūjāsatkāraṃ kṛtvā nānāgandhair nānāpuṣpair nānāvastraiḥ pariveṣayitvā caityasyopari dhvajāgrāvaropayitāṃ kṛtvā nānāvādyatūryasaṃgītibhir vādyamānābhiḥ pradakṣiṇīkartavyā / tatas teṣāṃ mahāsatvānāṃ yathā ciñcitam āśāṃ paripūrayiṣyanti / devatāḥ śakrabrahmaprabhṛtayaḥ / athavā yathāyathāvidhinā likhyate tathātathā samṛdhyate / putrārthī labhate garbhasaṃdhāraṇī parāḥ sukhena vardhate garbhaḥ sukhenaiva prasūyate / kālena vardhate garbhaḥ kālena parimucyate / kim iti mahābrāhmaṇa pūrvavac chrūyatām //
body.translated_text: be raised on the top of a banner and upheld. It pacifies all winds, cold spells, untimely clouds, lightning, and thunderbolts. It liberates from all disputes and conflicts among gods, humans, and non-humans. All kinds of biting insects, mosquitoes, <s>śarabhas</s>, and various living creatures that destroy crops are rendered powerless and are pacified. All hostile-minded wild beasts, birds, and fanged creatures are destroyed. All flowers, fruits, leaves, trees, medicinal herbs, and crops flourish abundantly. The tasteless becomes flavorful and tender. Everything ripens perfectly. The faults of excessive rain and drought will not occur at all. There will be timely rain, not untimely rain. The great <s>Nāgas</s> in that region will properly release the rain-streams at the right time. In whatever region this <s>Vidyārājñī Mahāpratisarā</s> is practiced — there the beings, having recognized it, should make offerings and reverence with various incenses, various flowers, and various garments, and having raised it on the top of a banner above a <s>caitya</s> (shrine), should circumambulate it with various musical instruments, drums, and songs. Then for those great beings, [the deities] headed by <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> shall fulfill their wishes as desired. Moreover, in whatever manner it is written according to the proper ritual, in that manner it succeeds. One who desires a son obtains a womb-retaining [charm]; the fetus grows with ease; the birth occurs with ease. The fetus grows at the proper time and is delivered at the proper time. How so, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>? Listen as before:

body.text: ihaiva magadhaviṣaye rājā prasāritapāṇir nāma sa cāputrako 'bhūva / kim iti prasāritapāṇir iti khyātān / tena rājñā jātamātreṇa pāṇiṃ prasārya mātuḥ stanau gṛhītvā yāvad āptaṃ kṣīraṃ pītam / tau ca stanau saha sparśamātreṇa suvarṇavarṇau saṃvṛttau / nityakālaṃ ca mahatā kṣīreṇa pravardhataḥ / tena kāraṇena tasya rājñaḥ prasāritapāṇir iti nāma sthāpitam / anyac ca tasya rājñaḥ yācanakajanā āgacchanti / tadā sa rājā dakṣiṇapāṇiṃ prasārayaty upary antarikṣe bodhisatvaḥ sa rājā tena hetunā tasya buddhābhiprasannā devatā divyai ratnaviśeṣaiḥ suvarṇamaṇibhiś ca pāṇiṃ paripūrayanti / tadā sa rājā tebhyo yācanakajanebhyo
body.translated_text: Here, in the region of <s>Magadha</s>, there was a king named <s>Prasāritapāṇi</s> (Outstretched Hand), and he was without a son. Why was he called <s>Prasāritapāṇi</s>? Because that king, at the very moment of birth, outstretched his hand, grasped his mother's breasts, and drank as much milk as he could obtain. Those two breasts, at the mere touch, turned the color of gold. They always abounded with copious milk. For that reason, the name <s>Prasāritapāṇi</s> was given to that king. Furthermore, when people seeking alms came to that king, the king would extend his right hand upward into the sky — that king being a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, for that reason the deities devoted to the <s>Buddha</s> would fill his hand with divine jewels and gold and precious gems. Then that king [would give] to those people seeking alms

body.text: 'nuprayacchanti / yathā cintamātreṇa sarvayācanakajanānāṃ sarvasukhasaṃpattikāmāṃ dadāti / devānāṃ ca mahānti pūjāsatkārāṇi karoti putrahetor na ca putraṃ pratilabhate / sa paurāṇāṃ tathāgatacaityānāṃ purataḥ pūjāsatkāraṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ / mahānti ca pūjāsatkārāṇi karoti dānāni ca dadāti / upavāsam upavasati / mahānti ca puṇyāni ca karoti / akṣiṇāny eva dānāni dadāti / tat kasya hetor bhūtapūrvaṃ mahābrāhmaṇa asminn eva magadhaviṣaye mallā nāma janapade kuśinagare mahāpaṭṭanavare bhagavataḥ prabhūtaratnasya tathāgatasya śāsane samutpanno dharmacittakaḥ kaścid mahāsatvo dharmamatir nāma śreṣṭhī prativasati / sa sarvasatvānām antike mahākaruṇācittam upasthāpya imām eva mahāvidyāṃ mahāpratisarām ārabhya dharmaṃ deśayati sma / atha kaścid eko daridrapuruṣas taṃ dharmaṃ śrutvā tasya śreṣṭhina idaṃ vacanam abruvat / aham āryasya niveśane bhṛtikarmaṃ kariṣyāmi dharmaṃ ca śroṣyāmi / yadā mama kiṃcid bhaviṣyati tadāhaṃ dharmaṃ pūjayiṣyāmi / tasya gṛhavyāpāraṃ kurvato dharmaṃ ca śṛṇvato yāvad apareṇa kālasamayena śreṣṭhinā eko dīnāro dattaḥ / sa tena sarvasatvaparitrāṇārthaṃ bodhicittam utpādya sādhāṛaṃ kṛtvā mahāpratisarāratneti niryātitā / evaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam anena mahāphalena mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca dāridraduḥkhasaṃcchedaḥ syāt / anena kāraṇena tad dānaṃ parīkṣayaṃ na gacchati / evaṃ bahuvidhānekavidhapuṇyābhisaṃskārakṛto devatāś ca pūjitā yāvad buddhā bhagavantaḥ pūjitās tadā ca śuddhāvāsakāyikābhir devatābhiḥ svapne darśanaṃ dattam / evaṃ cābhihitaṃ bho mahārāja samantajvālāmālāviśuddhisphūritacintāmaṇir mahāmudrāhṛdayāparājitā mahādhāraṇī mahāvidyārājñī mahāpratisarā nāma taṃ yathāvidhinā kalpenābhihitena upavāsoṣitāyā agramahiṣyā devyāḥ śarīre baddhā tatas te putrapratilambho bhaviṣyatīti / atha sa rājā prativiśuddhas tasyām eva rātryām atyayena saṃkhyālipinakṣatragrahavipañcakān kulabrāhmaṇān saṃnipātya yathāvidhinā
body.translated_text: they offer [gifts]. Just as, by merely thinking, [the wish-fulfilling gem] gives all happiness and prosperity to all those who make requests — [the king] performed great worship and honor to the gods and made offerings for the sake of a son, yet did not obtain a son. He began to perform worship and honor before the ancient <s>Tathāgata</s> shrines. He performed great worship and honor, gave gifts, observed fasting, performed great merits, and gave inexhaustible gifts. For what reason? In the past, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, in this very <s>Magadha</s> territory, in the land called <s>Mallā</s>, in the great city of <s>Kuśinagara</s>, under the teaching of the Blessed One <s>Prabhūtaratna Tathāgata</s>, there lived a certain great being, a guild-master named <s>Dharmamati</s>, who had arisen with a mind devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>. Having established a mind of great compassion toward all beings, he began to teach the <s>Dharma</s> based on this very great <s>vidyā</s>, the <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>. Then a certain poor man, having heard that <s>Dharma</s>, spoke these words to the guild-master: 'I will perform hired labor in the noble one's household and will listen to the <s>Dharma</s>. When I have something, then I will honor the <s>Dharma</s>.' While he was doing household work and listening to the <s>Dharma</s>, after some time the guild-master gave him one gold coin (<s>dīnāra</s>). With that, having generated the aspiration for awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) for the protection of all beings, he made it common [property] and offered it [saying] 'For the jewel of <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>.' He made this aspiration: 'By this great fruit, may there be the cutting off of the suffering of poverty for me and for all beings.' For this reason, that gift does not come to exhaustion. Thus, having performed manifold and various meritorious formations and worshipped the deities — and having worshipped the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> — then the deities of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> heaven gave him a vision in a dream, and spoke thus: 'O great king, the great <s>dhāraṇī</s>, the great queen of <s>vidyās</s> called <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>, the invincible heart-<s>mudrā</s> of the wish-fulfilling jewel radiating the garland of universal blazing purity — let it be bound upon the body of the chief queen who has observed a fast, according to the prescribed ritual. Then the obtaining of a son will come about for you.' Then that king, purified, at the passing of that very night, assembled <s>brāhmaṇas</s> of noble family [skilled in] numbers, writing, constellations, planets, and the five [arts], and according to the prescribed

body.text: kalpopadiṣṭena puṣye nakṣatrarāje pratipanne susnātagātrāyā upavāsoṣitāyā agramahiṣyā devyā yathāvidhinā likhyemāṃ mahāpratisarāṃ mahāvidyārājñīṃ kaṇṭhe baddhavān / mahatīṃ mahābuddhacaityeṣu pūjām akarṣīd anekāni ca ratnaviśeṣāṇi satvānāṃ dānāni dattāni / tato navānāṃ māsānām abhyayāt putro jāto 'bhirūpaḥ prāsādiko darśanīyaḥ / paramayā śubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgata iti //
body.translated_text: ritual, when the constellation <s>Puṣya</s>, king of constellations, had arrived, he wrote this <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>, the great queen of <s>vidyās</s>, according to the prescribed ritual, and bound it on the neck of the chief queen who had bathed well and observed a fast. He performed great worship at the great <s>Buddha</s>-shrines and gave many special jewels as gifts to beings. Then, after the passage of nine months, a son was born — handsome, graceful, pleasant to behold, endowed with the supreme beauty of auspicious complexion.

body.text: tato jñātvā mahābrāhmaṇa sarvakāmaṃgamā aparājitā mahāpratisarāratneti viśrutā mahāvidyārājñī sarvatathāgatapujitā śakrasyāpīyaṃ cūḍāmaṇiḥ sarvathā //
body.translated_text: Therefore know, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, that the invincible <s>Mahāpratisarā</s> jewel is renowned as the great queen of <s>vidyās</s> that fulfills all desires, worshipped by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and is in every way the crest-jewel even of <s>Śakra</s> himself.

body.text: yadā śakro devānām indro mahāsaṃgrāmam asuraiḥ sārdhaṃ kartukāmas tadā imāṃ mahāvidyāṃ kavacaṃ kṛtvā saṃgrāmamadhye 'vatīrya cūḍāyām avasthāpya sarvāsurān nirjitya sukhaṃ svastinā kṣemeṇa devapuraṃ praviśati / sarvāsurair adhṛṣyo bhaviṣyati / evaṃ hi mahābrāhmaṇa prathamacittotpādam upādāya boddhisatvasya mahāsatvasyemāṃ mahāpratisarāṃ mahāvidyārājñīṃ dhārayataḥ sarvamārair anavamṛdyatā bhavati / yasyaiṣā kaṇṭhagatā bhaviṣyati sa sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhito bhaviṣyati / sarvabuddhabodhisatvasaṃrakṣito bhaviṣyati / sarvadevamanuṣyāmanuṣyarājarājāmātyabrāhmaṇagṛhapatibhiś ca satatasamitaṃ vanditaḥ pūjitaḥ saṃmānito bhaviṣyati / sarvadevāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcitaḥ pūjito bhaviṣyati / sa mahāsatva ity uvāca / bhagavān mārabalapramardakaḥ sarvavyādhivigato bhaviṣyati / sarve 'tyupadravopasargāś cāsya praśāmyanti / tasya mahāsatvasya sarvaśokavigamo bhaviṣyati / sarvadevatāś cāsya satatasamitaṃ rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ vidhāsyanti / imāni cānena catvāry aparājitāmahāvidyāmantrapadahṛdayāni satatasamitaṃ likhitvā kāyakaṇṭhagatāni kṛtvā dhārayitavyāni / sasamitaṃ ca manasi kartavyāni / svādhyātavyāni bhāvayitavyāni cādhyāśayena sarvaduḥsvapnadurnimittāmaṅgalyabhāvā vinaśyanti / sarvasukhasaṃpattayaś ca prādurbhaviṣyanti /
body.translated_text: When <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, wishes to wage a great battle with the <s>asuras</s>, then making this great <s>vidyā</s> his armor, descending into the midst of battle, placing it on his crown, he conquers all <s>asuras</s> and enters the city of the gods happily, safely, and securely. He becomes invincible to all <s>asuras</s>. Thus indeed, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, from the first generation of the aspiration for awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>), for a <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>mahāsattva</s> who bears this <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>, the great queen of <s>vidyās</s>, there comes about invincibility by all <s>Māras</s>. Whoever has this placed upon the neck will be blessed by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, will be protected by all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, will be constantly saluted, honored, and revered by all gods, humans, non-humans, kings, ministers, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and householders, and will be worshipped and honored by all <s>devas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>. That great being — so spoke the Blessed One, crusher of <s>Māra</s>'s forces — will be free from all diseases. All calamities and adversities will be pacified for him. That great being will be free from all sorrow. All deities will constantly provide him with protection, shelter, and guardianship. And these four invincible great <s>vidyā</s>-<s>mantra</s>-word-hearts should be constantly written, placed upon the body and neck, and worn. They should be constantly kept in mind, recited, and cultivated with [sincere] intention — [then] all bad dreams, ill omens, and inauspicious conditions are destroyed, and all happiness and prosperity will manifest.

body.text: atra mantrapadāḥ siddhāḥ sarvakarmakarāḥ śrutāḥ //
body.translated_text: Here the <s>mantra</s> words are accomplished; they are heard as performers of all actions.
