body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ maṇidhari vajriṇi mahāpratisare hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā</s> // The subsidiary heart <s>vidyā</s> //

body.text: aśeṣaiḥ sarvabuddhair bodhisatvaiś ca śrāvakair ekasvarasaṃnipātena ekasvaranirghoṣeṇa imāni dhāraṇīmantrapadāni bhāṣitāni mahāpratisarāmahāvidyārājñīhṛdayakavacāny etāni mantrapattrapadāni sarvatathāgatadharmamudrayā mudritāni / atidullabham apy eṣāṃ śravaṇaṃ kiṃ punaḥ likhanapaṭhanadhāraṇavācanaparadeśanā buddhakṛtyam etad iti jñātavyā / iyaṃ hy atīva sarvapāpakṣayaṃkarā / sarvatathāgataiḥ praśaṃsitā anumoditā vyākṛtā paramadullabheyaṃ mahādhāraṇī aparājitā mahāpratisarā nāmadheyaṃ śravaṇam api paramadullabham / iyaṃ sarvapāpakṣayaṃkarī / mahābalaparākramā mahātejā mahāprabhāvā mahāguṇodbhāvanī sarvamārakāyikadevatāvidhvaṃsanakarī / sarvavāsanānusaṃdhisamudghāṭanakarī / sarvamārapāśasamucchedanakarī paramantramudrāviṣakākhordakiraṇaprayogavidveṣaṇābhicārakānāṃ ca duṣṭacittānāṃ vidhvaṃsanakarī / sarvabuddhabodhisatvāryagaṇavarapūjitābhiratānāṃ paripālanakarī / mahāyānodgrahaṇalikhanavācanapaṭhanasvādhyāyanaśravaṇadhāraṇābhiyuktānāṃ paripālikeyaṃ mahādhāraṇī yāvad buddhabodhiparipūrayitrīyaṃ mahābrāhmaṇa mahāpratisarā mahāvidyārājñī na kvacit pratijanyate sarvatra mahāpūjāṃ prāpnoti yathāhaṃ śāstā jitaviṣayaḥ / kim iti pūrvaṃ parijñātavatīyaṃ
body.translated_text: By all the <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>śrāvakas</s> without exception, in a single harmonious assembly with a single harmonious voice, these <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>mantra</s> words were spoken — these <s>mantra</s>-text words that are the heart and armor of the <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>, the great queen of <s>vidyās</s>, sealed with the <s>Dharma</s>-seal of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Extremely rare is even the hearing of these, let alone the writing, reading, retaining, reciting, or teaching them to others — this should be known as the activity of a <s>Buddha</s>. For this [<s>dhāraṇī</s>] is supremely the destroyer of all sins. Praised, rejoiced in, and prophesied by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, supremely rare is this great <s>dhāraṇī</s> called the Invincible <s>Mahāpratisarā</s> — even its hearing is supremely rare. This is the destroyer of all sins, of great strength and valor, of great brilliance, of great power, the manifester of great virtues, the destroyer of all deities of <s>Māra</s>'s retinue, the opener of all bonds of latent tendencies, the cutter of all <s>Māra</s>'s snares, the destroyer of those with malicious minds [who employ] hostile <s>mantras</s>, <s>mudrās</s>, poisons, sorcery, [evil] ray practices, and rites of enmity and black magic. She is the protector of those honored and delighted in by all <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and noble assemblies. This great <s>dhāraṇī</s> is the guardian of those devoted to taking up, writing, reciting, reading, studying, hearing, and retaining the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — and even the fulfiller of <s>Buddha</s>-awakening. O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, this <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>, the great queen of <s>vidyās</s>, is nowhere defeated; everywhere she obtains great worship — just as I, the Teacher, have conquered [all] domains. Why was this known before?

body.text: mahābrahmaṇa mahāvidyārājñī sarvavighnavināyakānāṃ vidhavaṃsayitrī //
body.translated_text: O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, this great queen of <s>vidyās</s> is the destroyer of all obstacles and <s>Vināyakas</s>.

body.text: yadā ca bhagavān vipulaprahasitavadanamaṇikanakaratnajvalaraśmiprabhāsābhyudgatarājas tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho yena bodhimaṇḍalas tenopasaṃkrānta upasaṃkramya sarvabuddhapraśastaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartayitukāmas tadā tasya bhagavataḥ sarvamāraiḥ saparivārair anekamārakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparivṛtair nānārūpavirūpabhayabhairavaśabdākulair bahuvividhamāraviṣayavikurvaṇādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitair nānāpraharaṇavṛṣṭībhir abhinirmāyāgatya caturdiśaṃ parivāryāntarāyaḥ kartum ārabdhaḥ / tataḥ sa bhagavān vipulaprahasitavadanamaṇikanakaratnajvalaraśmiprabhāsābhyudgatarājo muhūrtaṃ tūṣṇīm āsthāya imāṃ mahāpratisarāṃ mahāvidyārājñīṃ manasā saptakṛtvaḥ pravartayāmāsa / samanantaraṃ pravartayitāyām asyāṃ mahāpratisarāyāṃ mahāvidyārājñyāṃ tatkṣaṇād eva sarve te mārāḥ pāpīyāṃso dadṛśur bhagavata ekaikasmād romakūpavivarād anekakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi puruṣāṇāṃ saṃnaddhakavacānāṃ jvalitakhaṅgaparaśupāśamudgarāsimusaratriśūrahastānām evaṃ vācaṃ pravyāharamāṇāni gacchanti / gṛhṇata 2 bandhata 2 duṣṭamārān vidhvaṃsaya duṣṭacittān vicūrṇaya jīvitaṃ sarvaduṣṭagrahavighnavināyakānāṃ ye bhagavato viheṭhanaṃ kurvanti / tatas te sarvaduṣṭamārāmaitrīkhaṅgeṇābhinirjitāṃ kṛtvā kecic chikṣāpadāni grāhitā / kecid yāvad anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau vyākṛtās tatra mahānubhāvāḥ / anye punas tān tathāgataromavivaravinirgatān mahāpuruṣān dṛṣṭvā tasmin nagare vihvalībhūtā ṛddhiparihīṇā naṣṭapratibhānabalaparākramā vidhvastāḥ / samastāḥ samantāt prapalīnā iti / tato bhagavatā dharmacakraṃ prativartitam / yathānyair buddhair iti / sarvavighnavināyakān mārāṃś ca pāpīyāṃso vidhvaṃsayitvottīrṇaḥ pāraṃgata iti / evaṃ hi mahābrāhmaṇa mahābalavegarddhipāramitāprāpteyaṃ mahāpratisarā mahāvidyārājñī smaraṇamātreṇa sarvavyasanabhayabhairavebhyaḥ
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vipulaprahasitavadanamaṇikanakaratnajvalaraśmiprabhāsābhyudgatarāja</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly awakened one, approached the <s>Bodhimaṇḍala</s> and wished to set in motion the <s>Dharma</s> wheel praised by all <s>Buddhas</s>—at that time, all the <s>Māras</s> with their retinues, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Māras</s>, agitated with various terrifying and fearsome forms and sounds, empowered with many diverse miraculous transformations of <s>Māra's</s> domain, having manifested showers of various weapons and come from the four directions to surround him, began to create obstacles. Then that <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vipulaprahasitavadanamaṇikanakaratnajvalaraśmiprabhāsābhyudgatarāja</s>, having remained silent for a moment, mentally set forth this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s> seven times. Immediately upon this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s> being set forth, at that very instant all those evil <s>Māras</s> saw from each and every pore of the <s>Bhagavān's</s> body many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of men issuing forth, armored and armed, with blazing swords, axes, nooses, clubs, maces, spears, and tridents in hand, uttering these words: 'Go! Seize, seize! Bind, bind! Scatter the wicked <s>Māras</s>! Crush the evil-minded! Destroy the lives of all wicked <s>grahas</s> (seizers), obstacles, and <s>Vināyakas</s> who are tormenting the <s>Bhagavān</s>!' Then all those wicked <s>Māras</s>, having been conquered by the sword of lovingkindness (<s>maitrī</s>)—some were made to accept the rules of training, some of those great powerful ones were even given prophecy for unsurpassed perfect awakening. Others, seeing those great beings issuing forth from the <s>Tathāgata's</s> pores, became bewildered in that place, lost their supernatural powers, their eloquence, strength, and valor destroyed, were scattered and fled in all directions. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> set in motion the wheel of the <s>Dharma</s>, just as other <s>Buddhas</s> had done. Having scattered all obstacle-<s>Vināyakas</s> and evil <s>Māras</s>, he had crossed over and reached the other shore. Thus, O <s>Mahābrāhmaṇa</s>, this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s>, having attained the perfection of great power, force, supernatural ability, and strength, by mere recollection liberates from all calamities, fears, and terrors

body.text: parimocayati / āśayapariviśuddhānāṃ satvānāṃ nānyeṣāṃ duṣṭacetasām / tasmāt tarhi mahābrāhmaṇa nityam evānusmaraṇamātreṇa manasi kartavyā / sarvakālaṃ ca likhitvā kāyakaṇṭhagatāṃ kṛtvā dhārayitavyā / kim iti pūrvavac chrūyatām //
body.translated_text: —[but only] for beings whose intentions are purified, not for others who are evil-minded. Therefore, O <s>Mahābrāhmaṇa</s>, it should always be kept in mind by mere recollection. And having written it at all times, it should be worn on the body or around the neck. Why is that? Hear as before!

body.text: ujjayanyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ rājño brahmadattasya vihite kenacit puruṣeṇāparādhaḥ kṛtaḥ / sa rājñā brahmadattena vadhakapuruṣebhya ājñaptaḥ / bhavato gacchatainaṃ puruṣaṃ jīvitād vyaparopayateti / atha te vadhapuruṣās taṃ rājñājñaptaṃ puruṣaṃ gṛhītvā parvatavivaraṃ nītvā asikośān niṣkāsya taṃ puruṣaṃ jīvitād vyaparopayitum ārabdhaḥ / tadā sa puruṣa imāṃ mahāpratisarāṃ mahāvidyārājñīṃ manasā smṛtavān likhitāṃ ca dakṣiṇe bāhau baddhvā dhārayati sma / tasya mahāsatvasyāsyā mahāvidyāyāḥ prabhāvenāsir ekajvālībhūtā khaṇḍakhaṇḍaṃ yathā pāṃśumayo vikīrṇa iti / tatas te vadhakapuruṣā imam evaṃ niścayaṃ rājaṃ vistareṇārocayāmāsuḥ / tato rājā prakupitaś caṇḍībhūtaḥ kathayati / gacchata bho puruṣā anyatarasmin pradeśe yakṣaguhāsti / tatra bahūni yakṣaśatasahasrāṇi prativasanti piśitāśīni / tatra nītvā chorayata / tataḥ sa puruṣo vadhakapuruṣais tasyāṃ yakṣaguhāyāṃ choritaḥ / samanantara chorite tasmin yakṣaguhāyāṃ tatas te yakṣāḥ sarve tuṣṭamanaso hṛṣṭacittāś ca pradhāvitā mānuṣaṃ bhakṣayiṣyāma iti / te paśyanti asyā mahāpratisarāyā mahāvidyārājñyā anubhāvena taṃ puruṣam ekajvalībhūtaṃ dedīpyamānaṃ vigrahaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca sarva eva te yakṣā saṃtrastā dahyamānaṃ svaśarīraṃ paśyanti / atha te yakṣā vismayaṃ samāpannās taṃ puruṣaṃ gṛhītvā bahirdvāre 'vasthāpya pradakṣiṇīkartum ārabdhāḥ / yāvat tair vadhakapuruṣai rājñe niścayo 'yaṃ vistareṇāroitaḥ / tato bhūyo rājā prakupitaś caṇḍībhūtaḥ kathayati / yad eva bhavanto gacchatainaṃ puruṣaṃ baddhvā nadyāṃ prakṣipata / tataḥ sa puruṣo vadhakapuruṣair baddhvā nadyām prakṣiptaḥ / samanantaraṃ prakṣipte tasmin mahāpuruṣe sā nadī nirudakī bhūtā yatha sa
body.translated_text: In the great city of <s>Ujjayanī</s>, a certain man committed an offense against King <s>Brahmadatta</s>. He was ordered by King <s>Brahmadatta</s> to the executioners: 'Sirs, go and deprive this man of his life.' Then those executioners seized the man condemned by the king, led him to a mountain cave, drew their swords from their scabbards, and began to deprive him of life. At that time, that man mentally recalled this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s> and bore it written and tied upon his right arm. By the power of this great <s>vidyā</s> of this great being, the sword became a single mass of flame and shattered into pieces, scattered like dust. Then those executioners reported this matter in full detail to the king. Thereupon the king, enraged and fierce, said: 'Go, sirs! In a certain place there is a cave of <s>Yakṣas</s>. There many hundreds of thousands of <s>Yakṣas</s> dwell, flesh-eaters. Take him there and abandon him.' Then that man was abandoned by the executioners in that <s>Yakṣa</s> cave. Immediately upon his being abandoned in the <s>Yakṣa</s> cave, all those <s>Yakṣas</s>, delighted and joyful in mind, rushed forward [thinking]: 'We shall devour this human!' But they saw, by the power of this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s>, that man blazing as a single mass of flame, and seeing his radiant form, all those <s>Yakṣas</s> were terrified and saw their own bodies burning. Then those <s>Yakṣas</s>, filled with wonder, took that man, placed him outside the door, and began to circumambulate him. When the executioners reported this matter in full detail to the king, the king again, enraged and fierce, said: 'Then go, sirs, bind this man and throw him into the river.' Then that man was bound by the executioners and thrown into the river. Immediately upon that great being being thrown in, that river became waterless, so that

body.text: puruṣaḥ sthalagata eva tiṣṭhati / tāni ca bandhanāni khaṇḍakhaṇḍaṃ vicūrṇitāni / rājā śrutvā tato rājā vismitotphullavadanaḥ kathayati / aho vismayam idaṃ puruṣasya dṛśyate / kim atra kāraṇaṃ syād iti me vitarkaḥ / atha sa rājā taṃ puruṣam āhūyainam āha / kiṃ tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa jānāsi / sa puruṣa uvāca / nāhaṃ mahārāja kiṃcid api jānāmi / anyatra mahāpratisarāṃ mahāvidyārājñīṃ dhārayāmi / asyā eṣa deva mahāprabhāvaḥ / rājā āha / aho āścaryam idaṃ mahat / mahāvidyā subhāṣitā / mohanī mṛtyudaṇḍasya sarvabuddhair adhiṣṭhitā / tāraṇī sarvasatvānāṃ sarvaduḥkhapramocanī / mahāvidyā mahātejā akālamṛtyumocanī / bhāṣitā kāruṇikair nāthair mahāroganivāriṇī / tato rājñā prahṛṣṭamānasena mahāpratisarā mahāvidyārājñī pūjitā mānitābhinanditā / tasya puruṣasya poṭṭabandhaṃ kṛtvā svasya janapadasya purastān nagarajyeṣṭhatāyām abhiṣeko dattaḥ / evaṃ hi mahābrāhmaṇa iyaṃ mahāpratisarā mahāvidyārājñī sarvatra mahatīpūjāṃ labhate / anabhikramaṇīyā sarvaduṣṭacittaiḥ sarvaiḥ pūjanīyā / evaṃ hi mahābrāhmaṇa pūrvam iyaṃ mahāpratisarā mahāvidyārājñī na kvacit pratihanyate / tasmād avaśyam iyaṃ mahāvidyārājñī kāyakaṇṭhagatāṃ kṛtvā dhārayitavyā / api tu mahābrāhmaṇa manukṣetreṇeyaṃ mahāvidyārājñī supraśastena vidhānena likhitavyā //
body.translated_text: that man stood as though on dry land. And those bonds were crushed into pieces. The king, having heard this, with a face blossoming in amazement, said: 'What a marvel is seen in this man! What could be the reason for this?—such is my wonder.' Then that king summoned that man and addressed him: 'What is it that you know, sir?' The man replied: 'O great king, I do not know anything at all. I merely bear the <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s>. This, O lord, is its great power.' The king said: 'Ah, this is a great wonder! A great <s>vidyā</s>, well spoken! She bewilders the rod of death, empowered by all <s>Buddhas</s>! She is the deliverer of all beings, the liberator from all suffering! A great <s>vidyā</s> of great brilliance, she frees from untimely death! Spoken by the compassionate protectors, she wards off great diseases!' Then the king, with a joyful mind, honored, revered, and praised the <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s>. He bestowed upon that man a turban-binding [of honor] and consecrated him as governor of his own territory before the foremost citizens of the city. Thus, O <s>Mahābrāhmaṇa</s>, this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s> receives great worship everywhere. She is unapproachable by all evil-minded beings; she is to be worshipped by all. Thus, O <s>Mahābrāhmaṇa</s>, in former times this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s> was never obstructed anywhere. Therefore this <s>Mahāvidyārājñī</s> must be worn on the body or around the neck. Moreover, O <s>Mahābrāhmaṇa</s>, this <s>Mahāvidyārājñī</s> should be written with ink according to the well-established method.

body.text: atha sa mahābrāhmaṇo 'tīva prahṛṣṭamanasā bhagavantaṃ pañcamaṇḍalakenābhipraṇamya praṣṭum ārabdhaḥ / kīdṛśena bhadanta bhagavan vidhāneneyaṃ mahāpratisarā mahāvidyārājñī likhitavyā //
body.translated_text: Then that great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, with an exceedingly joyful mind, bowing down before the <s>Bhagavān</s> with the five-point prostration, began to ask: 'In what manner, O venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, should this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s> be written?'

body.text: bhagavān āha /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu mahābrāhmaṇa tvām ahaṃ vakṣye sarvasatvānukaṃpayā /
children.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Mahābrāhmaṇa</s>, I shall tell you, out of compassion for all beings,

children.text: yena satvāḥ sukhino bhontu mucyatai karmasaṃkaṭāt //
children.translated_text: by which beings may become happy and be freed from the distress of <s>karma</s>.
For the liberation of the afflicted, and for the arising of children in women's wombs,
there shall be for beings the overcoming of the veil of poverty.

body.text: upavāsoṣito bhūtvā nakṣatre puṣyasaṃmate /
body.translated_text: Having observed a fast, on the <s>nakṣatra</s> (constellation) approved as <s>Puṣya</s>,

body.text: buddhapūjāparo bhūtvā cittam utpācya bodhaye //
body.translated_text: having become devoted to the worship of the <s>Buddha</s>, generate the mind for awakening (<s>Bodhi</s>).

children.translated_text: With a mind saturated with compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), and also endowed with lovingkindness (<s>maitrī</s>),
and devoted to the welfare of all beings at all times,
having bathed with sandalwood, camphor, and musk-water,
putting on clean garments, fumigated with incense,
then, having prepared a <s>maṇḍala</s>, furnished with a horn [vessel],
draw the auspicious <s>maṇḍala</s> with five-colored powder.
Four full vessels, and a fifth in the center of the <s>maṇḍala</s>;

children.text: puṣpadhūpāś ca gandhāś ca dātavyātra mahārihā //
children.translated_text: flowers, incense, and fragrances of great value should be offered here.

children.text: dhūpanaṃ candanaṃ caiva spṛkkāguru tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: The incense should be sandalwood, <s>spṛkkā</s> (valerian), and <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood) as well;
five types of sugar and gold should be offered here according to the rite.
Various kinds of flowers, at the proper time and according to the proper method,
well-adorned with all flowers, fruits, seeds, and fragrances,
with ghee, honey, and milk, with fires and water-offerings and the like,

children.text: pūrayed balikumbhāś ca lakṣaṇād yān sumaṅgalān //
children.translated_text: one should fill the auspicious offering-vessels according to the prescribed marks,
and place [them] in the four directions, with a fifth in the center of the <s>maṇḍala</s>.
Bowls filled with fragrances should be placed at the corners.
And four pegs of <s>khadira</s> wood, firmly fixed,
should be fastened by the skilled with a five-colored thread,
and placed evenly, extending beyond the <s>maṇḍala</s>.

children.text: evaṃ kṛte likhed vipra yad icchet siddhim ātmanaḥ //
children.translated_text: Having done thus, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, one should write what one desires for one's own success.
One seeking happiness, having eaten pure food, should write

children.text: paṭṭe vā vastrabhūrje vānyatra vā yatra kutracit //
children.translated_text: on silk, on cloth, on birch bark, or elsewhere, wherever it may be.

children.text: likhet strīṣu ca putrārthī samyaggorocanena vai /
children.translated_text: One desiring a son should write on [amulets] for women with pure cow-bezoar (<s>gorocana</s>),
and in the center should make [the image of] a child adorned with all ornaments,
holding in the left hand a vessel filled with jewels,
seated on a beautifully blossoming lotus.
Jeweled necklaces, gold, and various special gems —

children.text: pravarṣaś cāpi kartavyāś catuḥ koṇeṣu parvatāḥ //
children.translated_text: and rain-clouds should be made at the four corners as mountains.

body.text: evaṃ likhet prayatnena yad icched jīvitaṃ sukham /
body.translated_text: Thus one should write with effort, if one desires a happy life.

body.text: kuṅkumena likhet prājñaḥ puruṣāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ //
body.translated_text: The wise one should write with saffron (<s>kuṅkuma</s>), especially for men.

children.translated_text: Their desired goals are accomplished — there is no doubt in this.

children.text: nānārūpāś ca kartavyā mudrācihnaś ca padminī //
children.translated_text: And various forms should be made, as well as seal-marks and lotuses.

children.text: dve padme athavā trīṇi catvāri pañca vā likhet /
children.translated_text: One should write two lotuses, or three, or four, or five,

children.text: padmānāṃ ca tathā kuryāt keśarāṇi samantataḥ //
children.translated_text: and should make filaments all around the lotuses.
One should make a well-blossomed lotus with a stem, bound with silk,
a trident on a lotus, and likewise a corner-piece bound with silk.

children.text: parśuṃ kuryāt tathā padme atha patre samantataḥ /
children.translated_text: One should make an axe on a lotus, and likewise leaves all around,

children.text: sakhaṅgaṃ padmaṃ kurvīta tat padmaṃ śitam eva ca //
children.translated_text: one should make a lotus with a sword, and that lotus should be sharp.

children.text: śaṅkhaṃ padme tathā kuryāt sarvatra vidhivistaram /
children.translated_text: One should likewise make a conch on a lotus, with full ritual elaboration everywhere,
the skilled one should have ritual marks made everywhere.
One should avoid crude forms where the mind becomes corrupted,
and divine forms should be made, adorned with various ornaments.

children.text: bhikṣuṃ vajradharaṃ kuryād duṣṭatarjanaṃ tat param /
children.translated_text: One should make a monk holding a <s>vajra</s>, as the supreme repeller of evil beings,

children.text: caturaś ca mahārājāṃś catuḥ pārśveṣu saṃlikhet //
children.translated_text: and should draw the four great kings (<s>Mahārāja</s>) on the four sides.
For <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Īśvara</s> should be written; for <s>kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>;

children.text: śūdreṣu ca sadā saumyaṃ cakrasvāminam ālikhet //
children.translated_text: for <s>śūdras</s>, one should always draw the gentle lord of the wheel (<s>Cakrasvāmin</s>);

children.text: vaiśyeṣu ca vaiśramaṇam indraś caiva sureśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: for <s>vaiśyas</s>, <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>; and <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods.
For children, <s>Prajāpati</s> of great wisdom should always be written.

children.text: syāmavarṇā bhaved yātu raudraṃ tasyā samālikhet /
children.translated_text: For a woman of dark complexion, one should draw a fierce [deity];
for a fair-complexioned one, one of beautiful form should always be written for those who are illustrious.
For a stout woman, <s>Māṇibhadra</s> should be written with care;

children.text: kṛṣāyāḥ pūrṇabhadras tu mayā hy uktaṃ svayaṃbhuvā //
children.translated_text: for a thin woman, <s>Pūrṇabhadra</s> — so I, the Self-Existent One (<s>Svayaṃbhū</s>), have declared.

children.text: gulviṇyāś ca mahākālo likhec ca brahmadevatān /
children.translated_text: For a pregnant woman, one should write <s>Mahākāla</s> and <s>Brahma</s> deities;
and for others, as before, one should draw what has been variously taught.
Having written with care, with the ritual procedure as prescribed,

children.text: dhārayet satataṃ kaṇṭhe bhadraṃ tasya bhaviṣyati //
children.translated_text: one should constantly wear it on the neck — auspiciousness will come to that person.
At the gateway, one should make a wish-fulfilling jewel (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>), placed on a lotus atop a banner,

children.text: padmasya keśare pāśaṃ cakraṃ cāpi tathāparam //
children.translated_text: and on the filaments of the lotus, a noose, and likewise a wheel.

body.text: vajraṃ padme tathā likhyaṃ mudgalaṃ padmasaṃsthitam /
body.translated_text: A <s>vajra</s> should likewise be drawn on a lotus, and a mace placed on a lotus,

body.text: śaktiṃ likhet tathā padme yathāvidhiṣu dṛṣyate //
body.translated_text: a spear should be drawn on a lotus, as seen in the ritual prescriptions.

children.translated_text: All the jewels at the gateway [should be] sparkling and clustered,
and they should be made bound with silk, as proclaimed in the ritual prescriptions.
<s>Nāgas</s> bearing fruit should be made at the jeweled gateway, with nine heads;
all of them, with care, established in the heart with <s>vajras</s>.

children.text: pārthivānāṃ balaṃ nityaṃ sārthavāhaṃ likhed budhaḥ /
children.translated_text: For kings, the wise one should always write [the image of] strength, and a caravan leader;
for all <s>vidyādharas</s>, one should draw a divine goddess.
The moon, sun, constellations (<s>nakṣatra</s>), <s>Rāhu</s>, <s>Ketu</s>, and the eight planets —

children.text: likhec ca khaṇḍāṃ pāṇḍānāṃ putralābho bhaviṣyati //
children.translated_text: one should draw them; for the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, the acquisition of a son shall come about.
Having written with certainty according to the method, with the ritual procedure seen in the treatise,
therefore, with all effort, a wise person should wear [this amulet].
For this is the accomplisher of all <s>siddhis</s>, auspicious, the destroyer of sins.

children.text: prāpnoti paramaṃ sthānaṃ svayaṃbhū vacanaṃ yathā //
children.translated_text: One attains the supreme state, as declared by the Self-Existent One (<s>Svayaṃbhū</s>).

children.text: loke 'smin paramaṃ saukhyaṃ paraloke paraṃ sukham /
children.translated_text: In this world, supreme happiness; in the next world, supreme bliss;
beginning with the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven, a place in the abode of the gods.

children.text: jambudvīpe śubhe ramye vidyāsaukhyaṃ ca nityaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the beautiful and delightful <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, the happiness of <s>vidyā</s> eternally.
Even all the <s>Buddhas</s> cannot fully proclaim the aggregate of merit
that the person who wears the <s>Pratisarā</s> obtains.
The doors of hell are shut; the doors of heaven are opened.
One will be endowed with happiness and prosperity, of great wisdom.

children.text: buddhāś ca bodhisatvāś ca āśvāsayanti nityaśaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> constantly give comfort.
Endowed with bodily happiness, one shall be of great strength.
As spoken by the <s>Jitendra</s> [the <s>Buddha</s>], one will become a wheel-turning monarch (<s>Cakravartin</s>).
A comfort to divine kings, a terror to those of evil mind —
such will one become in due time, for whom this <s>vidyā</s> is well recited.

children.text: nāsau hanyati śastreṇa na viṣeṇa nāgninā /
children.translated_text: One is not killed by weapons, nor by poison, nor by fire,
nor does untimely death [come]; evil ones flee far away.

children.text: darśanāt sparśanāc caiva śravaṇād eva sarvataḥ /
children.translated_text: By seeing, by touching, and by hearing — from all [directions],
disputes with spirit-possessors (<s>bhūtagraha</s>), and danger from water and fire,

body.text: mṛgāvyāḍāhayānāgāvyādhayaś ca sudāruṇāḥ /
body.translated_text: wild beasts, serpents, snakes, <s>nāgas</s>, and terribly severe diseases —

body.text: te sarve na bhaviṣyanti yeṣāṃ vidyā subhāṣitā //
body.translated_text: none of these shall befall those for whom this <s>vidyā</s> is well recited.

children.text: sarvathā sarvamārais tu śṛṇu vakṣāmi tatvataḥ /
children.translated_text: In every way, by all <s>Māras</s> — hear, I shall speak the truth:
they shall be honored, the supreme among all beings, for their welfare.

body.text: āryamahāvidyārājño mahāpratisarāyāḥ prathamakalpaḥ samāptaḥ //
body.translated_text: The first ritual chapter (<s>kalpa</s>) of the noble <s>Mahāvidyārājñī Mahāpratisarā</s> is complete.

body.text: athāto vidyāvarasya rakṣāvidhānakalpaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi sarvasatvānukampakayā /
body.translated_text: Now I shall explain the ritual chapter on the protective procedure of the excellent <s>vidyā</s>, out of compassion for all beings.

children.translated_text: By the protective procedure for people, great accomplishment (<s>siddhi</s>) shall come about.

children.text: yatra yatra kṛtā rakṣā bhavaty abaddho na saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Wherever protection is performed, there will be no bondage — there is no doubt.
Fearlessness, freedom from burning, and the warding off of all planetary [afflictions],
favorable constellations, and the cutting of the bond of <s>karma</s>.
Whatever has been wrongly eaten, wrongly transgressed, done by hosts of enemies,

children.text: duṣprekṣitaṃ dullikhitaṃ kākhordā ye ca dāruṇāḥ //
children.translated_text: wrongly looked upon, wrongly written, and those who are terrible sorcerers (<s>kākhorda</s>) —
and [spells] made with powdered mantras, poison consumed, and deadly toxins —

children.text: sarve tasya praśāmyanti rakṣāṃ dhāvayate tu yaḥ //
children.translated_text: all these are pacified for one who carries the protection.
Counter-spells (<s>pratyaṅgirā</s>) are rendered powerless for one who surpasses [all other] <s>vidyās</s>.
Even the terrible enemies of hostile forces, those of great danger,

children.text: sarve te pralapaṃ yānti pratisarā sāpatarjitāḥ /
children.translated_text: all of them are reduced to prattling, threatened by the <s>Pratisarā</s>.

children.text: buddhā rakṣanti sarvajñā bodhisatvāś ca pūratāḥ //
children.translated_text: The omniscient <s>Buddhas</s> protect, and the perfected <s>Bodhisattvas</s>,
the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> protect, and the <s>Śrāvakas</s> [who have overcome] great dangers.

children.text: anye ca bahuvidhā bhūyo devā nāgā mahārddhikāḥ //
children.translated_text: And many other diverse gods, <s>nāgas</s> of great supernatural power,

children.text: rakṣāṃ kurvanti tasyeme cāsmin yuktasya nityaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: all of these perform protection for one who is constantly devoted to this.
By the mere hearing of this <s>vidyārājñī</s>, O best of men,

children.text: nirbhayo bhavati sarvatra ity evaṃ munir abravīt /
children.translated_text: one becomes fearless everywhere — thus spoke the <s>Muni</s>.

children.text: duḥsvapnā duṣkṛtā ye ca upasargā ye ca dāruṇā //
children.translated_text: Bad dreams, evil deeds, and terribly dangerous afflictions,
those struck by disease, great illnesses, those seized by royal birth [troubles],
and many other diverse diseases — boils, spider-bites, eczema,

body.text: itayo dāruṇā ye ca grasante mānuṣīṃ prajām /
body.translated_text: terrible calamities that seize the human race,

body.text: manuṣyāṇāṃ vināśārthaṃ hiṃsakāś ca sudāruṇāḥ //
body.translated_text: and terribly harmful ones [that work] for the destruction of humans —

children.text: sarve te pralapaṃ yānti rakṣā yatra mahābalāḥ /
children.translated_text: all of them are reduced to prattling where this mighty protection exists.
One who has performed protection with this [<s>vidyā</s>], even when condemned to death, is freed.
Even if seized by the noose of <s>Kāla</s> (death) and led to the abode of <s>Yama</s>,
one's lifespan increases even by the writing of the <s>Pratisarā</s>.

children.text: parikṣīṇāyuṣo yas tu saptāhamṛta eva ca /
children.translated_text: For one whose lifespan has been exhausted, even dead for seven days,

children.text: yāval likhitamātreṇa sa jīvati na saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: by the mere writing [of the <s>Pratisarā</s>], that person lives — there is no doubt.
And by mere hearing, with protection performed according to the prescribed method,

children.text: svasti prāpnoti sarvatra sukhaṃ jīvati cepsayā //
children.translated_text: one attains well-being everywhere and lives happily as desired.
Sixty-eight thousand, and hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s>,

children.text: trāyastriṃśāś ca ye devā sarve śakrapurogamāḥ //
children.translated_text: and the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, all led by <s>Śakra</s>,
for the protection of that being, stand behind [them].
The four world-protectors (<s>Lokapāla</s>) and <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> of great strength,

children.text: vidyā kulaśataiḥ sārdhaṃ rakṣāṃ kurvanti nityaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: together with hundreds of <s>vidyā</s> families, constantly perform protection.

children.text: somaḥ sumatāḥ sūryaś ca brahmā viṣṇur maheśvarāḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Soma</s>, <s>Sumatā</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>,

children.text: yamaś ca māṇibhadraś ca baladevo mahābalaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s>, <s>Māṇibhadra</s>, <s>Baladeva</s> of great strength,
<s>Pūrṇabhadra</s> the great hero, and <s>Hārītī</s> with her children,
<s>Pāñcāla</s>, <s>Pāñcika</s>, <s>Kārtikeya</s>, <s>Gaṇeśvara</s>,

children.text: śrīr api ca mahādevī vaiśramaṇaḥ sarasvatī //
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> the great goddess, <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
<s>Śaṅkhinī</s>, <s>Kūṭadantī</s>, and likewise <s>Ekajaṭā</s>,

children.text: dhanyā etā mahābhāgā rakṣāṃ kurvanti nityaśaḥ //
children.translated_text: these blessed ones of great fortune constantly perform protection.
She is a giver of sons to the barren, a promoter of the growth of the womb.

children.text: rakṣeyaṃ mahatī cāsya yāvad jīvaṃ bhaviṣyati //
children.translated_text: This great protection will be for one as long as one lives.
She constantly gives victory to men in terrifying battles and conflicts.
By this [<s>vidyā</s>], the deities firm in <s>Dharma</s> become boon-givers.

children.text: atha pāpavināśe tu likhanād eva setsyati /
children.translated_text: And in the destruction of evil, success will come from merely writing it.
The <s>Tathāgatas</s> will look upon him, and the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> likewise.

children.text: yaśaś ca vardhate tasya puṇyam āyuś ca vardhate /
children.translated_text: His fame will increase, and his merit and lifespan will grow.

children.text: dhanadhānyaṃ samṛddhiś ca bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Wealth, grain, and prosperity will arise — there is no doubt.

body.text: sukhaṃ svapiti medhāvī sukhaṃ ca pratibudhyate /
body.translated_text: The wise one sleeps happily and awakens happily.

body.text: adhṛṣyaḥ sarvaśatrūṇāṃ sarvabhūtagaṇair api //
body.translated_text: He is invincible to all enemies and to all hosts of <s>bhūtas</s> as well.

children.translated_text: For one engaged in battle, victory will always come.
When a <s>vidyā</s> (spell) is being accomplished, this is the supreme protection.

children.text: sukhaṃ sādhayate vidyāṃ vighno 'sya na bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: One accomplishes the <s>vidyā</s> with ease, and no obstacle will arise for him.
All ritual procedures succeed, and he enters all <s>maṇḍalas</s>.

children.text: kṣipraṃ ca samayajño 'sau bhavet sarvatra jātiṣu /
children.translated_text: Quickly he becomes one who knows the pledge (<s>samayajña</s>) in all his births.

children.text: vaisvāsikaś ca sa bhavej jinānāṃ guṇadhāraṇaiḥ //
children.translated_text: And he becomes a trusted one of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones) through the retention of their qualities.
Endowed with all auspiciousness, all accomplishments, and the fulfillment of desires,
by the mere writing of this, all happiness is achieved.
Having made a happy death, he becomes one whose destiny is heaven.
In disputes, quarrels, and in the most terrible conflicts,
he is freed from all fear, according to the word spoken by the <s>Jina</s>.

children.text: nityaṃ jātismarā bhonti jātau na saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: They will always possess memory of past births in every birth — there is no doubt.
Kings become subject to his will, along with the great people of the inner court.

children.text: sāmātyaś ca bhaven nityaṃ sādhubhir lokasamataiḥ //
children.translated_text: Together with ministers, he will always be among the virtuous and the world-honored.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ ca priyo bhonti ye devā ye ca mānuṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: He becomes dear to all, whether <s>devas</s> or humans.

children.text: rakṣāṃ tasya kariṣyanti divā rātrau ca nityaśaḥ //
children.translated_text: They will perform his protection day and night, constantly.

body.text: atra mantrapadāḥ siddhāḥ samyaksaṃbuddhabhāṣitāḥ /
body.translated_text: Herein are the accomplished <s>mantra</s> words, spoken by the Perfectly Awakened One.

body.text: namo buddhāya / namo dharmāya / namaḥ saṃghāya //
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>! Homage to the <s>Dharma</s>! Homage to the <s>Saṅgha</s>!

body.text: namo bhagavate śākyamunaye mahākāruṇikāya tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya /
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Bhagavān Śākyamuni</s>, the greatly compassionate <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One!

body.text: namaḥ samantebhyaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhebhyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Homage to all the Perfectly Awakened Ones everywhere!

children.translated_text: Having paid homage through meditation, for the growth of the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching,
I shall now proclaim, out of compassion for beings,
this <s>vidyā</s> of great brilliance, of great power and valor,
which, upon being merely spoken by the Sage with the <s>vajra</s> noose,

children.text: mārāś ca mārakāyāś ca grahāḥ sarve vināyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Māras</s> and the hosts of <s>Māra</s>, all <s>grahas</s> (seizers), and <s>Vināyakas</s> (obstacle-makers),

children.text: vighnāś ca santi ye kecit tatkṣaṇād vilapaṃ gatāḥ //
children.translated_text: and whatever obstacles exist — all instantly perish.

body.text: tadyathā / oṃ giri 2 giriṇi 2 girivati guṇavati ākāśavati / ākāśaviśuddhe / ākāśe / gagaṇatale / ākāśavicāriṇi / jvalitaśikhare /
body.translated_text: The formula is as follows: <s>oṃ giri giri giriṇi giriṇi girivati guṇavati ākāśavati</s>, O one purified in space, O space, O surface of the sky, O one who roams through space, O blazing-peaked one,

body.text: maṇimauktikhacitamaulivare sukeśe / suveśe / suvaktre sunetre / suvarṇe suvarṇagaure / atīte / anāgate / pratyutpanne / namaḥ sarveṣāṃ buddhānāṃ jvalitatejasām / buddhe subuddhe / bhagavati surakṣaṇi / sukṣeme suprabhe / sudame sudānte / vare varade / bhagavati bhadravati / bhadre subhadre / vimale jayabhadre / caṇḍe pracaṇḍe / caṇḍi 2 vajracaṇḍe ghori gandhāri gauri caṇḍāli mātaṅgi varcasi / sumati / pukkasi / śavari śāvari / śaṃkari dramiḍi drāmiḍi raudriṇi / sarvārthasādhani /
body.translated_text: O one with a crest studded with jewels and pearls, O beautiful-haired one, O beautifully adorned one, O beautiful-faced one, O beautiful-eyed one, O golden one, O one with a golden fair complexion! In the past, in the future, in the present — homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> of blazing splendor! O awakened one, well-awakened one, O <s>Bhagavatī</s>, O great protectress, O one of great security, O supremely radiant one, O well-tamed one, well-disciplined one, O excellent one, O boon-granter, O <s>Bhagavatī</s>, O auspicious one, O auspicious one, well-auspicious one, O stainless one, O victorious and auspicious one! O fierce one, exceedingly fierce one, O fierce one, fierce one, O <s>vajra</s>-fierce one! O terrifying one, <s>Gandhārī</s>, <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Caṇḍālī</s>, <s>Mātaṅgī</s>, <s>Varcasī</s>, <s>Sumatī</s>, <s>Pukkasī</s>, <s>Śavarī</s>, <s>Śāvarī</s>, <s>Śaṃkarī</s>, <s>Dramiḍī</s>, <s>Drāmiḍī</s>, <s>Raudriṇī</s>! O accomplisher of all purposes!

body.text: hana 2 sarvaśatrūn / daha 2 sarvaduṣṭān pretapiśācaḍākinīnāṃ manuṣyāmanuṣyāṇāṃ ca / paca 2 hṛdayaṃ vidhvaṃsaya jīvitaṃ sarvaduṣṭagrahāṇāṃ nāśaya sarvapāpāni me bhagavati / rakṣa 2 māṃ saparivāraṃ sarvasatvāṃś ca sarvatra sarvadā sarvabhayopadravebhyaḥ sarvaduṣṭānāṃ bandhanaṃ kuru 2 sarvakilbiṣanāśani / mārtaṇḍe mṛtyudaṇḍanivāriṇi mānini / cale vicale / ciṭi 2 viṭi 2 niṭi nituṭe / ghoriṇi vīriṇi / pravarasavare / caṇḍāli / mātaṅgi / rundhasi / varcasi / sumati pukkasi / śavari śāvari / śaṃkari dramiḍi drāmiḍi / dahani / pacani pācani / mardani / sarale 2 saralaṃbhe / hīnamadhyotkṛṣṭavidāriṇi / mahile 2 mahāmahile / nigaḍe 2 nigaḍabhañje / matte / maṭṭini / dānte / cakre cakravākini / jvale 2 jvālini / śavari śāvari sarvavyādhiharaṇi / cūḍi 2 cūḍini 2 mahācūḍini / nimi 2 nimindhari / trilokadahani / trilokālokakari / traidhātukavyavalokani / vajraparaśupāśamuṅgarāsicakratriśūlacintāmaṇimahāvidyādhāriṇi / rakṣa 2 māṃ sarvasthānagataṃ sarvaduṣṭabhayebhyaḥ sarvamanuṣyāmanuṣyabhayebhyaḥ sarvabhayebhyaḥ sarvavyādhibhyaḥ / vajre vajravati vajrapāṇidhare / hili 2 mili 2 kili 2 cili 2 sili 2 vara 2 varade /
body.translated_text: Strike, strike all enemies! Burn, burn all evil-doers — the <s>pretas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>ḍākinīs</s>, humans and non-humans! Cook, cook! Shatter their hearts! Destroy the lives of all malevolent <s>grahas</s>! Destroy all my sins, O <s>Bhagavatī</s>! Protect, protect me together with my retinue and all beings, always and everywhere, from all fears and calamities! Create bonds, create bonds for all evil-doers, O destroyer of all offenses! O <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s> (sun), O averter of the rod of death, O proud one! O moving one, wildly moving one! <s>ciṭi ciṭi viṭi viṭi niṭi nituṭe</s>! O terrifying one, O heroic one! O one supreme among the excellent! O <s>Caṇḍālī</s>, <s>Mātaṅgī</s>, O subduer, <s>Varcasī</s>, <s>Sumatī</s>, <s>Pukkasī</s>, <s>Śavarī</s>, <s>Śāvarī</s>, <s>Śaṃkarī</s>, <s>Dramiḍī</s>, <s>Drāmiḍī</s>! O burner, O cooker, O tormentor, O crusher! O straight one, straight one, O one with a straight lance! O destroyer of the low, middling, and exalted! O great one, great one, O supremely great one! O shackle, shackle, O breaker of shackles! O intoxicated one, O crushing one, O tamed one! O wheel, O one with the wheel! Blaze, blaze, O blazing one! O <s>Śavarī</s>, <s>Śāvarī</s>, O remover of all diseases! O topknot, topknot, O topknotted one, topknotted one, O great topknotted one! <s>nimi nimi nimindhari</s>! O burner of the three worlds! O illuminator of the three worlds! O surveyor of the three realms! O bearer of the great <s>vidyā</s> of <s>vajra</s>, axe, noose, mace, sword, wheel, trident, and wish-fulfilling jewel! Protect, protect me in all places from all fears of evil-doers, from all fears of humans and non-humans, from all fears, and from all diseases! O <s>vajra</s>, O <s>vajra</s>-bearing one, O one who holds the <s>vajra</s> of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>! <s>hili hili mili mili kili kili cili cili sili sili</s>, O excellent one, excellent one, O boon-granter!

body.text: sarvatra jayalabdhe svāhā / sarvapāpavidāriṇi svāhā / sarvavyādhihariṇi svāhā / saṃbharaṇi svāha / sarvaśatrubhayahariṇi svāhā / svastir bhavatu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca svāhā / śāntiṃkari svāhā / puṣṭiṃkari svāhā / balavardhani svāhā / oṃ jayatu jaye
body.translated_text: To the one victorious everywhere, <s>svāhā</s>! To the destroyer of all evil, <s>svāhā</s>! To the remover of all diseases, <s>svāhā</s>! To the gatherer, <s>svāhā</s>! To the remover of the fear of all enemies, <s>svāhā</s>! May there be well-being for me and for all beings, <s>svāhā</s>! To the maker of peace, <s>svāhā</s>! To the maker of nourishment, <s>svāhā</s>! To the increaser of strength, <s>svāhā</s>! <s>oṃ</s>, may the victorious one conquer, O victorious one,

body.text: jayavati kamale vimale svāhā / vipule svāhā / sarvatathāgatamūrte svāhā / oṃ bhūri mahāśānti svāhā / oṃ bhūri 2 vajravati sarvatathāgatahṛdayapūraṇi āyuḥsaṃdhāraṇi / bala 2 balavati jaya vidye hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā / oṃ maṇidhari vajriṇi / mahāpratisare hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā //
body.translated_text: O victorious one, O lotus, O stainless one, <s>svāhā</s>! O vast one, <s>svāhā</s>! O embodiment of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! <s>oṃ bhūri</s>, great peace, <s>svāhā</s>! <s>oṃ bhūri bhūri</s>, O <s>vajra</s>-bearing one, O fulfiller of the heart of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, O sustainer of life! Strength, strength, O powerful one! O victorious <s>vidyā</s>, <s>hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā</s>! <s>oṃ</s>, O jewel-bearer, O <s>vajra</s>-holder, O <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>, <s>hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā</s>!

body.text: yasya kasyacit mahābrāhmaṇa anayā tathāgatamūrtyā vidyāmantrapadadhāriṇyā rakṣā kṛtā guptiḥ paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntiḥ svastyayanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraḥ śastraparihāro viṣadūṣaṇaṃ viṣanāśanaṃ kṛto bhavet /
body.translated_text: O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, for whomever protection, guarding, safeguarding, sheltering, watching over, peace, well-being, averting of punishment, averting of weapons, neutralizing of poison, and destruction of poison has been performed through this <s>vidyā-mantra</s> formula that is the embodiment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>,

children.text: tasya parīkṣīṇām āyuḥ punar eva vivardhate /
children.translated_text: for that person, even an exhausted lifespan increases once again.

children.text: suciraṃ sukhaṃ jīvati smṛtisaṃpannaś ca bhavati //
children.translated_text: One lives happily for a long time and becomes endowed with mindfulness.

body.text: uccāraṇamātreṇa vajrāvamarjanena vā akālamaraṇāt mahāvyādhibhyaś ca parimucyate / sarvarogāś cāsya praśāmyanti / dīrghamlānāny avamārjanamātreṇa praśamaṃ gacchanti / dine dine svādhyāyaṃ kuryān mahāprājño bhavati / ojobalavīryapratibhānasaṃpanno bhavati / sarvakarmāvaraṇāni cāsya niyatavedanīyāni niravaśeyaṃ parikṣayaṃ gacchanti / sarvabuddhabodhisatvadevanāgayakṣādīni cāsya ojobalavīryaṃ kāye prakṣepsyanti / mahāprītir bahulo bhaviṣyati / antaśo mahābrāhmaṇa iyaṃ mahāvidyāmantrapadarakṣā tiryagyonigatānām api mṛgapakṣiṇāṃ yeṣāṃ karṇapuṭe vipatite sarve vaivarttikā bhaviṣyanty anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / kaḥ punar vādo ya imāṃ mahāpratisarāṃ dhāraṇīṃ śrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bhikṣur vā bhikṣuṇī vā upāsako vā upāsikā vā rājā vā rājaputro vā rājāmātyo vā brāhmaṇo vā kṣatriyo vā tad anyo vā yaḥ kaścic chrokṣati śrutvā ca mahatyā śraddhayā gauraveṇādhyāśayena likhiṣyati likhāpayiṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati / tīvreṇa manasā bhāvayiṣyati / parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyati / tasya mahābrāhmaṇāṣṭau akālamaraṇāni pratikāṃkṣitavyāni na prabhavanti / na cāsya kāye mahāvyādhayo bhaviṣyanti / nāgnir na viṣaṃ na śastraṃ na garaṃ
body.translated_text: By the mere utterance, or by the <s>vajra</s> cleansing, one is liberated from untimely death and great diseases. All his ailments are pacified. Long-standing afflictions are pacified by the mere cleansing. If one recites it daily, one becomes greatly wise. One becomes endowed with vitality, strength, vigor, and eloquence. All his obstructions due to karma, even those with certain retribution, are completely exhausted without remainder. All the <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and others will infuse vitality, strength, and vigor into his body. Great joy will be abundant. Finally, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, this great <s>vidyā-mantra</s> word of protection — even for beings born in animal realms, for animals and birds, into whose ear-cavities it should fall — they will all become irreversible (<s>avaivartika</s>) in the supreme perfect awakening. What need then to speak of a faithful son or daughter of good family, a <s>bhikṣu</s> or <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, a male or female lay follower, a king or prince, a royal minister, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> or <s>kṣatriya</s>, or anyone else, who will hear this great <s>Mahāpratisarā dhāraṇī</s>, and having heard it, will write it, cause it to be written, retain it, recite it with great faith, reverence, and sincere intention, meditate upon it with an intense mind, and proclaim it in detail to others? For that person, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the eight kinds of untimely death are to be expected to have no power. Nor will great diseases arise in his body. Neither fire, nor poison, nor weapons, nor harmful substances

body.text: na kākhordā na kiraṇā na mantrakarmaṇaṃ na cūrṇayogo nāṅgaśūlaṃ na śirovarti ekāhikaṃ dvaitīyakaṃ cāturthakaṃ saptāhikā vā jvālā na kramiṣyanti / sa smṛta eva sukhaṃ svastinā svapiti / smṛta eva vibudhyate / mahāparinirvāṇalābhī bhaviṣyati / sakṛtsahadharmeṇa mahad aiśvaryaṃ cādhigacchanti / sa yatrayatropapadyate tatratatra jātau jātau jātismaro bhaviṣyati / sarvasatvānāṃ ca priyo bhaviṣyati / vandanīyaś ca pudgalo bhaviṣyati / sarvanarakagatitiryagyonigatigaṇapretopapattibhyaś ca parimukto bhaviṣyati / yathā cārkamaṇḍalaṃ sarvasatvānāṃ tathā raśmyāvabhāsakaro bhaviṣyati / yathā candramaṇḍalam amṛtena prabhavatā sarvasatvānāṃ kāyaṃ prahradayati tathā dharmāmṛtena sarvasatvānāṃ cittasantānāni prahradayiṣyati / sarvaduṣṭayakṣarākṣasabhūtapretapiśāconmādāpasmāraḍākinīgrahavighnavināśakādayaḥ sarve 'sya mahāpratisarāyā mahāvidyāyāḥ prabhāvena na śaktā viheṭhanāṃ kartum / upasaṃkrāmatāṃ ca teṣām iyaṃ mahāvidyārājñī smartavyā / tatas te sarve duṣṭacittā vidyādharasya vaśyā ājñayā śravaṇavidheyā bhaviṣyanti / asyā evānubhāvena yad uta mahāpratisarāyā mahāvidyārājño na cāsya śatrubhayaṃ bhaviṣyati / anatikramanīyaś ca bhaviṣyati / sarvaśatrugaṇai rājamahārājāmātyabrāhmaṇagṛhapatibhiś ca / antaśo vadhyārho 'pi vadhakapuruṣair ucchritāny api śastrāṇi khaṇḍaṃ khaṇḍaṃ gacchanti pāṃśumayānīva viśīryas tataś ca samaye sarvadharmā asyābhimukhī bhaviṣyanti / mahac cāsya smṛtibalaṃ bhaviṣyanti /
body.translated_text: Neither <s>kākhordā</s> (sorcery), nor [malevolent] rays, nor mantra-rites, nor poison-mixtures, nor body-pain, nor headache, nor one-day fevers, two-day fevers, four-day fevers, or seven-day fevers shall assail [the bearer]. Being mindful, one sleeps in comfort and well-being. Being mindful, one awakens. One shall attain the great <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. By the very same <s>dharma</s>, one attains great sovereignty. Wherever one is reborn, in each and every birth, one shall remember one's past lives. One shall be dear to all beings. One shall be a person worthy of reverence. One shall be freed from rebirth in all hells, animal realms, hungry ghost realms, and assemblies of <s>pretas</s>. Just as the disk of the sun illuminates all beings with its rays, so shall one illuminate. Just as the disk of the moon gladdens the bodies of all beings with its arising nectar, so shall one gladden the mind-streams of all beings with the nectar of the <s>Dharma</s>. All hostile <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>bhūtas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, madness-demons, epilepsy-demons, <s>ḍākinīs</s>, and obstacle-destroying <s>grahas</s> — all these, by the power of this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyā</s>, are unable to cause harm. When they approach, this <s>Mahāvidyārājñī</s> should be recalled. Then all those hostile-minded beings shall become subject to the <s>vidyā</s>-holder's command and obedient to his orders — through the very power of this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s>. Nor shall there be danger from enemies. One shall be inviolable by all hosts of enemies, kings, great kings, ministers, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and householders. Even if one deserves execution, the weapons raised by the executioners shall break into pieces as if made of dust, and at that moment all <s>dharmas</s> shall be favorable to that person. Great power of mindfulness shall be theirs.

children.text: rakṣoghnaṃ paramaṃ hy etat pavitraṃ pāpanāśanam /
children.translated_text: This is the supreme destroyer of <s>rākṣasas</s>, the purifier, the annihilator of sin,
the bestower of fortune, the bestower of wisdom, and the enhancer of all virtues.
It is the creator of all auspiciousness and the destroyer of all inauspiciousness,
the shower of good dreams and the destroyer of bad dreams.
This <s>vidyā</s> is the supreme protection for both women and men, possessing great power.
In forests, wilderness, and difficult terrain, they are instantly freed at that very moment.

body.text: sarvakāmāṃś ca labhate buddhasya vacane yathā //
body.translated_text: One obtains all desires, in accordance with the word of the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: patha utpatham āpannā eṣāṃ vidyām anusmaret //
body.translated_text: Those who have gone astray from the path should recall this <s>vidyā</s>.

children.text: panthānaṃ labhate śīghraṃ bhojanaṃ pānam uttamam /
children.translated_text: One quickly finds the path, food, and supreme drink.

children.text: karmaṇā manasā vācā yat kṛtaṃ pūrvajanmasu //
children.translated_text: Whatever was done by action, mind, or speech in previous births —
any and all unwholesome deeds of various kinds shall be exhausted.

children.text: smaraṇād dhāraṇāc caiva udgrahāl likhanād api //
children.translated_text: Through recollection, through retention, through mastery, and through writing,
through recitation, through utterance, through chanting, and through teaching to others,
one shall before long attain the course of all <s>dharmas</s>.

children.text: evaṃ hi dharmarase prāpte pāpā gacchanti saṃkṣayam /
children.translated_text: When the essence of the <s>Dharma</s> is thus obtained, sins go to destruction.

children.text: sidhyante sarvakarmāṇi manasā yad yad īpsitam //
children.translated_text: All actions are accomplished; whatever is wished for in the mind.
In all fears of death, there shall be protection for that person.

children.text: rājāgnir udakaṃ caiva vidyud vā taskaro 'pi vā //
children.translated_text: From the king, from fire, from water, from lightning, or from thieves,
from battles, clashes, and quarrels, and from fierce fanged beasts —

children.text: sarve te pralapaṃ yānti vidyāyā lakṣajāyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: all those flee lamenting, born from the hundred-thousandfold [recitation] of the <s>vidyā</s>.

children.text: vidyemāṃ paramāṃ siddhāṃ sarvabuddhair hi deśitā /
children.translated_text: This supreme, perfected <s>vidyā</s> has been taught by all <s>Buddhas</s>.
Those who glorify it do not fail in fulfilling the accumulation of awakening.

children.text: sarveṣu caiva sthāneṣu imāṃ vidyāṃ prayojayet /
children.translated_text: In all places, one should employ this <s>vidyā</s>,
for whatever tasks are desired, for the accomplishment of one's own and others' aims.
They are accomplished effortlessly through the <s>vidyā</s> — there is no doubt in this.

children.text: namaḥ sarvatathāgatebhyo ye 'pi tiṣṭhanti daśasu dikṣu //
children.translated_text: Homage to all <s>Tathāgatas</s> who abide in the ten directions!

body.text: oṃ maṇivajre hṛdayavaire mārasainyavidāriṇi hana 2 sarvaśatrūn rakṣa 2 mama śarīraṃ sarvasatvānāṃ ca vajre 2 vajragarbhe 2 / trāsaya 2 sarvamārabhavanāni hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ maṇivajre hṛdayavaire mārasainyavidāriṇi hana hana sarvaśatrūn rakṣa rakṣa mama śarīraṃ sarvasatvānāṃ ca vajre vajre vajragarbhe vajragarbhe / trāsaya trāsaya sarvamārabhavanāni hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā</s> //

body.text: buddhamaitrīsarvatathāgatavajrakalpādhiṣṭhite sarvakarmāvaraṇāny apanaya svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>Buddhamaitrīsarvatathāgatavajrakalpādhiṣṭhite sarvakarmāvaraṇāny apanaya svāhā</s> //

children.translated_text: Now I shall proclaim the healing treatment for the afflicted.
One should make a square <s>maṇḍala</s> prepared with earth and cow dung.
With five-colored powders, one should draw the auspicious <s>maṇḍala</s>.

children.text: caturaḥ pūrṇakuṃbhāṃś ca sthāpayed vidhinā budhaḥ //
children.translated_text: The wise one should place four full water-vessels according to the ritual.

body.text: puṣpāṇy avakiret tatra dhūpayed dhūpam uttamam /
body.translated_text: One should scatter flowers there and burn the finest incense.

body.text: balikarmaṃ ca kurvīta mahāsāhasrapramardanam //
body.translated_text: One should perform the <s>bali</s>-offering, the great crushing of a thousand-fold [obstacles].

children.translated_text: As before, one should offer fragrances, flowers, and the like according to the prescribed method.

children.text: caturas tīrikāḥ sthāpyāḥ sarvāś ca paṭṭabaddhakāḥ //
children.translated_text: Four torch-stands should be placed, all bound with cloth.
Having then placed the afflicted person, wrapped in clean garments,
with body anointed with auspicious fragrances, one should lead them into the center of the <s>maṇḍala</s>.
Seated facing east, one should recite this <s>vidyā</s>.

children.text: saptaso japtayā cāsya rakṣāṃ kuryād vicakṣaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: The skilled one should perform the protection by reciting it seven times.
Then, for the sake of the afflicted, twenty-one times
one should recite this <s>vidyā</s> for the pacification of all diseases.

children.text: bhūyaś ca saptavārān vai varikumbhaṃ sumantritam /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) should consecrate the water-vessel with seven recitations,
and afterwards place the water and flowers according to the proper method.

children.text: ity evaṃ dakṣiṇe pārśve prakṣipet sapta eva tu /
children.translated_text: Thus on the right side, one should cast exactly seven [times],

children.text: paścimā yāntu saptaiva uttarāyāṃ tathā diśi //
children.translated_text: on the western [side] exactly seven, and likewise on the northern direction,

children.text: adha ūrdhvaṃ tu saptaiva kṛtā rakṣā bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: below and above exactly seven — the protection shall be accomplished.
When this is done, O best of twice-born, one is freed from all suffering.

children.text: eṣā rakṣā mayā khyātā śākyasiṃhena bhāṣitā /
children.translated_text: This protection, proclaimed by me, was spoken by the Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>.

children.text: nāsty asyāḥ parā kācid rakṣā vidyā tridhātuke //
children.translated_text: There is no protection or <s>vidyā</s> higher than this in the triple realm.

body.text: na tasya mṛtyur na jarā na rogo na ca priyair jātuviyogabhāvaḥ / na cāpriyais tasya hi saṃprayogo bhaved dhiyo bhāvitacittasaṃtatiḥ / yamo 'pi tasya varadharmarājā kariṣyate pūjāṃ sagauraveṇa / kathayiṣyate devasuraṃ hi gacha kṣaṇikaṃ mamedaṃ narakapurajvāriṃ kariṣyasi / tato vimānaiḥ subahuprakārarir maharddhiko yāti surālayaṃ śubham / evaṃ hy asau naramarudyakṣarākṣasaiḥ saṃpūjitas tatra sadā bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: For that person there is no death, no old age, no disease, nor ever the state of separation from the beloved, nor indeed any association with the unpleasant — for one whose mind-stream is cultivated with wisdom. Even <s>Yama</s>, the excellent Dharma-King, shall perform worship for that person with reverence, saying: 'Go to the realm of gods and <s>asuras</s>! You shall momentarily act as the gate-keeper of my hell-city.' Then, in magnificent <s>vimānas</s> (celestial chariots) of many kinds, the one of great supernatural power goes to the beautiful celestial abode. Thus shall that person always be worshipped by humans, <s>Maruts</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: vajrapāṇiś ca yakṣendra indra caiva śacīpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the lord of <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>Indra</s>, the lord of <s>Śacī</s>,
<s>Hārītī</s> and <s>Pāñcika</s>, and the world-protectors (<s>Lokapāla</s>) of great supernatural power,
the moon and sun together with the constellations, and the planets that are most terrible,

children.text: te ca sarve mahānāgā devatā ṛṣayas tathā //
children.translated_text: and all those great <s>Nāgas</s>, deities, and <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) likewise,

children.text: asurā garuḍā gandharvāḥ kinnarāś ca mahoragāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and great serpents (<s>Mahoragas</s>) —
they constantly [guard] the one of great <s>vidyā</s>-power for the sake of Buddha-protection.

children.text: likhitāṃ dhārayet prājño bāhau baddhvā maharddhikāḥ /
children.translated_text: The wise one of great supernatural power should write it and wear it bound on the arm.

children.text: mahatīṃ labhate pūjāṃ saṃpadaṃ cāpi nityaśa iti //
children.translated_text: One constantly obtains great worship and prosperity.

body.text: mahāpratisarāyā vidyārājño rakṣāvidhānakalpo vidyādharasya samāptaḥ //
body.translated_text: The ritual procedure (<s>kalpa</s>) of protection for the <s>vidyā</s>-holder from the <s>Mahāpratisarā Vidyārājñī</s> is complete.
